## v1611 · 02-Oct-2026 IST

User: could not log in as admin - "Firebase: The current environment does not support the specified persistence type (auth/unsupported-persistence-type)". Sign-in set Firebase persistence from Remember me (SESSION when off) and stopped when the phone refused it. Now the wanted type is tried, then LOCAL, SESSION and NONE, and sign-in always continues. No data or Firebase cost change. Functions: dvSetPersistence (new), doFacultyLogin, doFirebaseLogin, _ensureAuth.

User: the staff widget stayed linked to Admin when a faculty member tapped its Link button. A widget tap counted as a plain login, and a plain login never moves a widget that shows someone else (v1574 rule). ## v1604 · 02-Oct-2026 IST

Bug (faculty: Lesson plan showed "No LP data in portal DB" after refresh; Link to me could not move the staff widget from admin; logout did not free it): the DB2 / DB4 sign-in tokens kept since v1592 / v1588 were treated as valid 1 h from when they were handed over, but Firebase can hand over a cached token already near its end, so expired tokens failed DB2 / DB4 reads and writes quietly. Tokens now use their real expiry (JWT exp, renewed if under 5 min left), and any DB2 / DB4 request refused with 401/403 gets a fresh token and is retried once. No extra reads. Functions: _jwtExp, _lpTokReset (new), fetch retry wrapper, _lpGetPortalToken, _lpGetArchiveToken.

## v1600 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

THE START-UP FREEZE (user: slow since hostel/canteen). Reproduced locally with the real app + Firebase SDK and 450 students: one 49 s main-thread block; CPU profile: the v1554 hostel-name marker (tag / norm / TreeWalker.nextNode) = 46 s. It walked all ~120,000 text nodes of the page (85,773 elements, every hidden panel) on every DOM change and in one go. Now it marks only on-screen content (active panel, header, sidebar, popups), checks the text length before normalizing, works in idle slices of at most ~8 ms, and marks a panel when it is opened (switchPanel -> hcTagVisible). Display only, no data change. The automatic one-run profiling (v1596) is switched off; the hostel timing line and its Profile button stay. Pairs with portal v10.51 (same marker fix). Functions: the 🏨 marker (tag, pump, check, tagVisible), switchPanel, hcTimingShow.

## v1599 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

Fix (v1598 network timing: davan_logo_2026.gif was 12,378 KB): the college logo GIF was 400x400 px, 400 frames at 20 fps, looping, shown at 32-72 px in several places at once (sidebar, headers, brand logos, loaders) - decoding it kept the phone's main thread busy (~15 s freezes, everything else waited). Replaced in place, same file name, with a 96x96 px, 200-frame, 10 fps version (1.1 MB); student_portal.html, results.html and library.html use the same file and get the fix too. No data change. Files: davan_logo_2026.gif.

## v1598 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

Fix (v1596 profile: the phone froze ~15 s twice on every open while Firestore reads were pending, all answered right after; no app function slow): Firestore app_data/students (549 KB) is read at login over Firestore's REST API with the signed-in user's token (same rules) and plain JSON.parse instead of the Firestore library, whose conversion of that document runs on the main thread. Any failure falls back to the normal read. Same 1 read. Functions: fsGetFast, _fsRestVal (new), loadFirestoreData.

## v1592 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

Bug (from the v1591 hostel timing line): the hostel dashboard's staff widget box took 52 s. Its one tiny DB2 read waited for the DB2 sign-in: at start-up many DB2 reads ran at once and each started its own anonymous sign-in (rate-limited). The DB2 token is now shared by all callers, kept across app opens for 1 h (localStorage lp2_tok), and the saved sign-in is awaited (max 3 s) before signing in again - every DB2 read in the app benefits. Same fix as v1588 for DB4. Functions: _lpGetPortalToken, hswGet (timing).

## v1591 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

User: the opening progress bar did not move and the hostel dashboard was slow. (1) Since the v1581 split the page code loads in ~1 s, and the opening screen closed 200 ms after that - before sign-in or data - so its steps never moved. It now follows the real loading (signed in, student data loaded, then closes; at most 6 s after sign-in, 15 s overall) and the bar shimmers and creeps between steps. (2) The hostel dashboard records where its time goes (DB4 sign-in, each read with size and time, drawing, staff widget box) - admin sees it at the bottom of the dashboard (tap to expand), everyone in the console. ## v1581 · 01-Oct-2026 IST

User: the app is still very slow to open and the welcome bar does not move, although the databases are fine. Measured at phone CPU speed: the page spent ~2 s frozen reading and compiling 4.5 MB of code written inside index.html (on every open) plus 1.7 MB of Excel / PDF libraries loaded before the app could start. Now index.html is BUILT from src/index.src.html by tools/build_index.js: big scripts go to js/admin-<n>-<hash>.js with comments removed (2.75 MB instead of 4.5 MB, kept compiled by the phone, a new hash on every change), and xlsx-js-style / html2pdf / jspdf / autotable load in the background 20 s after opening (an early export tap shows "tap again in a moment"). Result in tests: ready 2.9 s -> 1.3 s, frozen 2.0 s -> 0.6 s, longest freeze 0.6 s -> 0.18 s, same behaviour and no errors. Also: the "Widget update available" banner reads this phone's Davan Staff report (davan_pub/staff_widget_report/<S- code>, 1 small read) so it no longer shows w132 for people on w145. Functions: dvLibs (new), wcpReadOwnApkReport.

## v1515 · 28-Sep-2026 IST

System Log cleanup + two real listener bugs, from the admin System Log. (1) [WidgetSync] PERMISSION_DENIED on davan_pub/widget_active_user: doFirebaseLogout() fired davanWidgetSync(null,null) WITHOUT await and signed out straight away, so the widget logout writes ran after the token was revoked (widget could keep showing the old user). ## v1512 · 28-Sep-2026 IST

BUG FIX - Tidy grids / Delete grid did not stick: deleted grids (e.g. III BCOM, III BCA B, III BBA, 1 bba, I YEAR B.Com (from live)) came back after a reload. ROOT CAUSE: tgSave() saved app_data/tg_staging through fsSet(), which always used Firestore set(data, {merge:true}); merge keeps nested map keys that the new data no longer has, so every grid removed from TG_STATE.grids / liveGrids and every class-day removed from assign/liveAssign stayed in Firestore, and tgLoad()s Firestore catch-up put them back. FIX: fsSet() takes opts {replace:true} (plain set, whole document) and tgSave() uses it for tg_staging - TG_STATE is always saved whole, so nothing is lost. All other fsSet() callers unchanged (still merge). Verified with a Firestore-semantics simulation using the real fsSet code: before = deleted grid back after reload; after = stays deleted. NEEDS ONE MORE Tidy after this update (the stale grids are still in Firestore until the next save). FILES (index.html): fsSet 10762; tgSave replace call 30703; CODE_BUILD 18210.

## v1484 · 23-Sep-2026 IST

REAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND, after admin correctly rejected a wrong theory this session was building ('what all u r thinking is wrong ... think properly') and a live, step-by-step F12 trace was carried through to its actual conclusion instead. Earlier in this same session, a chain of reasoning was building toward 'the RTDB mirror is stale because app.py never writes to it' as the fix, and had gotten as far as asking admin for DB1's real RTDB URL to patch app.py — admin's pushback stopped that before any code was written on that theory, which turned out to be the right call: the ACTUAL bug was one line away, already inside index.html, not in app.py at all. LIVE-TRACED WITH REAL DATA, not assumed: a real manager login's own F12 console showed allStudents (404 students, loaded successfully) had 'Software Engineering' with NO int1 field at all for a real student (Vinay D.M), while the SAME student's SAME subject in admin's session showed a real value. Traced the data's actual origin: manager's copy came from RTDB davan_pub/students, savedAt 2026-09-22T13:23:21 — genuinely stale, predating the app.py v085 faculty-suffix-matching fix. But rather than stop at 'stale RTDB, patch the scraper to sync it', the NEXT real question was asked and tested directly: does Firestore ITSELF actually work for this real manager login right now? A direct db.collection('app_data').doc('students').get() call from the SAME real manager session returned exists:true, 404 students, updatedAt 2026-09-22T20:01:51 — hours NEWER than the RTDB mirror — and the SAME student's Software Engineering entry correctly showed int1:'AB', the real answer. CONCLUSION, proven not assumed: Firestore is NOT actually blocked for manager on this real deployment, contradicting a long-standing assumption repeated across many changelog entries in this file since v1339 ('Firestore blocks on file:// origin for manager/ VP') — that assumption may have been true on some earlier device/deployment this app once ran on, but is demonstrably false for this login, right now, proven with two live, back-to-back real reads from the SAME session. THE ACTUAL BUG: [loadFirestoreData() index.html ~10558] unconditionally skipped Firestore entirely for manager/vp/ principal BEFORE ever attempting it, routing straight to _loadFromRTDB() (davan_pub/students, a manual-'Sync to Cloud'-button-only mirror, confirmed by reading app.py directly — the scraper itself never writes any RTDB path on the DB1/davan-attendance-2026 project at all, only on the separate DB2/DB4 projects for Lesson Plan data) — so manager was permanently locked onto a snapshot that only updates when someone remembers to click a specific button, regardless of how fresh Firestore's real data actually was. This function ALREADY HAD a complete, correct try/catch fallback mechanism below the skip (checks for a genuine permission-denied error code, falls back to RTDB/localStorage safely) — the bug was never giving that mechanism a chance to run, by bailing out before the first attempt. FIX: removed the pre-emptive role check entirely — every role now genuinely attempts Firestore first via the existing, already-correct try/catch, and falls back to RTDB only on a REAL failure, never a guessed one. FIX: imInit() now uses Promise.all([imLoadExcludedRemote(), imReloadAndRefresh()]).then(()=>imRender()) — both loads run in parallel as before (no added wait time) but imRender() is called exactly once, only after BOTH have genuinely finished, removing the race entirely rather than guessing which one should win. imReloadAndRefresh() no longer calls imRender() internally during the imInit() sequence (tracked via a new _imReloadInSequence flag) but still renders correctly on its own when the admin clicks the manual '🔄 Reload Data' button directly, which bypasses imInit() entirely and needs its own render as before. The Promise.all() fix above already guarantees the panel never renders before the real remote data has loaded, so an instant-paint local cache served no purpose it did not already create as a liability. ## v1456 · 22-Sep-2026 IST

REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED, confirmed by direct admin console dump: the v1454/v1455 diagnostics conclusively proved the isolate-subject click logic was always correct (right cells matched, right styles applied, styles genuinely persisted) -- the actual bug was that opacity set on the <td> was never visually inherited by the <input> element inside it. The admin's own dump showed it directly: the td's computed opacity correctly read 0.16, but the input child's own computed opacity read 1, full visibility, despite having no opacity of its own set anywhere -- form controls are commonly rendered as their own independent compositing layer by the browser and do not reliably inherit an ancestor's opacity the way plain text or divs do. This is why every subject's text stayed fully legible in the admin's screenshot even though the JS was demonstrably doing exactly what it was supposed to. FIX: _tteHighlightSubject() now also sets opacity directly on the cell's own <input> (and its .tte-fullsubject/.tte-facname label divs, which have the same inheritance risk) in all three states -- reset, isolated-match, and dimmed -- not just on the parent <td>. Both diagnostic console.log blocks added across v1453-v1455 to investigate this are now removed; the function is back to a clean, minimal shape with only the real fix added. ## v1439 · 19-Sep-2026 IST

REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED, confirmed by an actual Firestore error the admin captured directly from the browser console: "FirebaseError: Function DocumentReference.set() called with invalid data. Unsupported field value: undefined (found in field _realGridsDuringSwap in document app_data/tg_staging)" -- this was surfacing correctly as the "⚠ not synced" indicator the admin then (rightly) asked about, which is itself a genuine, working, honest status feature (v1396) doing exactly its job: reporting a real cloud-save failure rather than hiding it. ROOT CAUSE #1: v1434's fix used Object.assign(..., { _realGridsDuringSwap: undefined, ... }) to strip two internal scratch fields before persisting -- verified AT THE TIME that JSON.stringify() correctly omits undefined-valued keys (true, and correct for the localStorage.setItem() write), but fsSet() passes the object DIRECTLY to Firestore's own .set() method WITHOUT going through JSON.stringify() first -- and Firestore's SDK explicitly REJECTS any field holding a literal undefined value, unlike JSON.stringify's silent-drop behavior. So the localStorage save always succeeded while the Firestore save always failed, for every single live-editor edit since v1434 shipped. FIX: use actual `delete` to remove the two scratch keys entirely, instead of setting them to undefined -- a genuinely absent key is fine for both persistence paths. ROOT CAUSE #2, a SEPARATE race condition found and fixed in the same pass via a direct async-timing simulation before trusting the first fix alone: tgSave() is async and does `await fsSet(...)`, but none of the 16 grid-editing *Impl functions await tgSave()'s own returned promise -- so tgWithLiveEditorGrids()'s `finally` block (which deletes TG_STATE._realGridsDuringSwap/_realAssignDuringSwap) runs SYNCHRONOUSLY the instant tgSave() is merely CALLED, not after it actually finishes. Reading those two fields LATER in tgSave()'s own function body (after its own await had already yielded control back to the caller) could read them as already-deleted/undefined from this race alone, reproducing the identical Firestore error through a completely different mechanism than root cause #1, even with #1 already fixed. Confirmed directly: a standalone simulation without the fix showed the scratch field already gone by the time it was read; the same simulation WITH the fix showed it correctly still present. FIX: tgSave() now captures _tgSavingLiveEditorGrids and both true grids/assign values as its very FIRST synchronous statements, before anything else in the function runs (including the scheduled-snapshot re-sync block, which also needed the true values and was updated to use this same snapshot) -- guaranteed to run before the caller's finally block gets a chance to fire, since JavaScript never yields control mid-way through a run of synchronous statements. VERIFIED: 21 script blocks node --check clean; div-balance confirmed unchanged at the established +2 baseline; a full end-to-end simulation reproducing the EXACT race (unawaited async save, real setTimeout-based delay standing in for the real Firestore round-trip) confirms the correct data (Times' true grids, not the live editor's) is now written successfully with no error, whereas the same simulation without either fix reproduces the exact reported failure. CODE_BUILD=1439.

## v1427 · 19-Sep-2026 IST

REAL BUG FOUND, affecting ALL THREE click-to-isolate grids, confirmed by direct Node testing of the actual production regex rather than assumption -- per admin report + 3 screenshots showing lab clicks still not highlighting in Faculty Schedule AND clicks doing nothing at all in Edit Timetable and View Timetable Class View. FIX: switched the separator from whitespace to a literal pipe character (|), which cannot appear in any real subject code -- all 5 K/H value-construction sites ("K/H HIN"/"K/H KAN HIN") converted to pipe-joined ("K/H|HIN"/"K/H|KAN|HIN"), and all 3 .split(/\s+/) read sites (_tteHighlightSubject, _ttvHighlightSubject, _ttvFacHighlightSubject) converted to .split('|'). Multi-word single-value bases (lab codes, "ADAP - LAB", etc.) are now correctly treated as one atomic value in every one of the three grids, while the real K/H multi-value case continues working exactly as before (verified: KAN, HIN, and K/H itself all still correctly match against a "K/H|KAN|HIN" cell). FIX, two parts working together: (1) tgGridFor(cls, day) no longer defaults to 'std' -- it returns null when nothing has been explicitly assigned, full stop. A new tgHasAssignment(cls) checks whether ANY day has a real assignment. (2) A new tgWithDraftOneClass(cls, fn) swaps LM_SLOTS_ORDER to ONLY that one class's own axis (via the existing tgAxisForClass, which itself now benefits from tgGridFor's honest null) for the duration of rendering that single class's section -- replacing the old shared-axis tgWithDraftAll() call in the build loop. Every class is now rendered inside its own tgWithDraftOneClass() call: classes on different grids can never see each other's columns, and a class with tgHasAssignment(cls) === false renders a collapsed placeholder ('No time grid assigned yet -- set one in Assign grid per day above') instead of a fabricated table. The Assign-grid-per-day dropdowns gained an honest '-- not set --' option (shown/selected whenever tgGridFor returns null) instead of silently pre-selecting Standard; tgSetDayGrid() correctly handles clearing an assignment back to unset. ## v1381 · 12-Sep-2026 IST

FEAT: SCHEDULED CHANGEOVER for Time Grids (v1380). Admin correctly reported that the flow he asked for was not in the v1380 build: the Effective from date was saved to TG_STATE.effectiveFrom but nothing ever read it, so the only real action was Archive & activate, which fired immediately. The intended flow is archive the present timetable, build the new one, keep it ready, set a date such as 1 Dec, and have the old timetable stop and the new one appear on that date. WHAT WAS ADDED: tgSchedule() freezes a deep COPY of the current draft (grids + assign) against the chosen date into TG_STATE.scheduled / TG_STATE.scheduledFor, after running the same clash validation activation uses. Editing the draft afterwards does NOT leak into what was scheduled -- what goes live on the day is exactly what was reviewed when it was scheduled, which has to be changed by an explicit re-schedule. tgPromoteIfDue() runs from tgApplyOnLoad() on every load, does nothing unless a schedule exists AND tgTodayISO() has reached tgFmtDate, then swaps the frozen copy into place and commits through tgCommit(), the exact same path manual activation uses. tgCancelSchedule() clears the date and keeps the draft. tgActivate() remains as an Activate now override that skips the date entirely. HONEST LIMITATION, STATED TO ADMIN: this is a client-side PWA with no server or cron, so nothing can wake up on the date by itself. The changeover fires the first time the ADMIN app is opened on or after the date -- if nobody with admin opens it that morning, the push to faculty/students/widget waits until someone does. Making it fire with nobody opening anything would require pushing both versions with the date and teaching each client to choose, which means student portal changes AND an APK rebuild; that was deliberately NOT done here so this stays a single-file change. A countdown banner (SCHEDULED -- new timings go live on DD Mon YYYY, N day(s) away / CHANGEOVER DUE) makes the pending state visible on the Times tab so it cannot be silently forgotten. DATE SAFETY: tgTodayISO() builds the date from local getFullYear/getMonth/getDate parts and never uses .toISOString(), which has already caused 2+ shipped UTC/IST off-by-one-day bugs in this file (stuParseCalDate, calSaveEvent). GUARD: if the scheduled version turns out to contain a faculty clash when the day arrives, promotion is REFUSED rather than silently applied, the schedule is retained so it can be fixed, and a 12-second toast tells the admin to open Edit Timetable then Times. TEST HARNESS BUG WORTH RECORDING (not a shipped bug): the first scheduler test run reported the clash guard failing. The cause was the test extracting the TG module by scanning to the next banner comment, which over-ran the module boundary and swallowed the real let LM_TIMETABLE = [] declaration that sits just below it; the harness rewrote let to var and thereby reset the test timetable to empty, so validation had no rows to find. ## v1380 · 12-Sep-2026 IST

FEAT: TIME GRIDS (TG) -- per-class, per-day period structures with staged activation, built in one pass per admin instruction. WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY: slot times were hardcoded in LM_SLOTS_ORDER and referenced by STRING in ~45 downstream sites (ttBuildGrid, ttBuildGridTransposed, ttBuildFacultyGrid, ttBuildFacultyOnlyGrid, ttBuildSubjectIndexGrid, _ttPrintClassGrid, renderFacultyTT, lmGetSubstitutes, dutySlotSession, extractSlotsFromHeader, LCB and the Excel import/export). Rather than rewriting all of them, LM_SLOTS_ORDER was changed from const to let and is now DERIVED: tgApplyOnLoad() replaces it with the union of every active grid's slot strings, sorted by real clock minute. Every existing consumer keeps iterating LM_SLOTS_ORDER unchanged and keeps working; when all classes share one grid the union is byte-identical to the old hardcoded array, so nothing changes until grids actually diverge. CRITICAL GUARD -- CLASH DETECTION: faculty double-booking was previously free because identical slot STRINGS collided. The moment two classes use different grids, Class A 09.30-10.30 and Class B 09.15-10.15 are different strings that overlap in real time, so string matching would silently report no clash while a faculty is physically in two rooms. tgValidate() therefore compares real minute intervals, never slot names, and tgActivate() is BLOCKED on any overlap. REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING BUILD (caught by testing against actual LM_TT_DEFAULT, not a rewrite): the first remap implementation mapped rows by position among filled periods. I YEAR BCA (A) has no morning classes -- its Monday starts at 11.45 -- so position mapping compressed its whole day into the first periods and silently moved it to the morning. tgRemapTimetable() now maps by INDEX on the class+day's OLD slot axis (tgOldSlotsFor, from TG_STATE.lastActive, falling back to LM_SLOTS_ORDER on first activation), which preserves free-period gaps. Rows whose index exceeds the new grid are reported as drops in the preview before anything is committed; rows whose slot is not on the old axis are left untouched rather than guessed at. SAFETY: everything writes only to staging (davan_tg_staging in localStorage, davan_pub/tg_staging in RTDB, app_data/tg_staging in Firestore). Live behaviour is untouched until Archive & activate is pressed, which first snapshots the current timetable, allocations and slot axis to davan_pub/tg_archive (restorable via Restore archive), then remaps, rebuilds the slot axis and pushes the flattened result to davan_pub/timetable. Portal and widget payload SHAPE is unchanged, so neither the student portal nor the Android widget needs any code change or APK rebuild for this feature. UI: new Times tab beside Grid/List in Edit Timetable -- named reusable grids, add/remove/edit periods, per-day grid assignment per class with a copy-to-other-days prompt, effective-from date, live preview of the resulting slot axis, and Preview & check which lists clashes and drops before activation. VERIFIED: 25 automated checks run under TZ=Asia/Kolkata against the real LM_TT_DEFAULT (253 rows) -- time parse/format round-trip on all 8 real slots, 12-hour afternoon resolution (01.15 = 795 min), union reproducing LM_SLOTS_ORDER exactly, no-op remap being an identity, gap preservation for afternoon-only classes, pure 30-minute shift losing no rows, drop counting on an 8-to-3 shrink, interval-overlap clash detection across grids sharing no slot string, and no false positive on disjoint intervals. NOT verified by automation: the interactive UI path (clicking through the tab and pressing activate) was render-checked only. CODE_BUILD=1380.

VERIFIED: all 20 real script blocks node --check clean (block 0 pre-existing false positive, confirmed unrelated, same as every prior entry); confirmed all 6 touched functions have exactly one definition each and every real caller (iaeEditCutoffDate, iaeSaveWindowsUI, iaeGrantPermission, iarAutoApplyBatch, iarSetTA, and the two log-append call sites) still receives the same boolean shape it expected before, no caller signature changes needed. THIS EXPLAINS the exact reported symptom precisely: rule-clears (iarAutoApplyBatch, called automatically on every Final Shortage page-open, likely mostly triggered from admin's own Firestore-unblocked session) kept logging fine, while manual permission grants (disproportionately performed by principal/manager/vp -- Firestore-blocked roles, per this file's own long-documented constraint) were silently dropped from the timeline specifically. FIX: table width changed to width:100% PLUS a computed min-width ((forScreen?4:3)*90 + sheet.columns.length*75, i.e. the fixed Sl No/Photo/URN/Name columns plus 75px per real date column, matching the 70px min-width already set on each individual date <th>) -- same min-width-scales-with-column-count pattern this file already uses elsewhere for exactly this many-dynamic-columns problem (see the existing Excel-View table at index.html ~38456, which sizes off subjects.length the same way). A table with few real columns still fills the container as before (min-width simply stays below 100%); a table with many real columns (like this admin's 13-column case) now correctly forces its true content width, so the wrapper's overflow-x:auto scrollbar has real width to scroll across instead of nothing to trigger it. SCOPE: only the Room Master Sheet's table touched -- the room-wise Attendance/Signature Sheet's own table (a fixed ~6-7 column layout, never grows with the Internal's real slot count) was confirmed NOT to have this problem and was deliberately left unchanged. PDF/Print were also confirmed unaffected -- jspdf-autotable computes its own real column widths independent of this CSS and already showed every column correctly; this was purely an on-screen View rendering bug. VERIFIED: all 20 real script blocks node --check clean (block 0 pre-existing false positive, confirmed unrelated); confirmed via direct grep that only the ONE table style rule reported by this admin (Room Master Sheet, ~line 63205) was touched, the sibling room-wise sheet's table style (~line 62992) is untouched and intentionally left as-is. ## v1359 · 08-Sep-2026 IST

CRITICAL FIX -- ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE of every visiting-field corruption tonight (idx 2, 5, 7 fragments -- all the same failure, not separate bugs). Firestore does NOT support dot-path field updates INTO array elements: .update({'visiting.7.dob': val}) does not mean 'array index 7's dob field' -- Firestore arrays are a distinct type, not a numeric-keyed map, so this silently REPLACES the entire visiting field with a new one-entry map {'7':{dob:val}}, discarding the real array completely. Every earlier fix tonight (array-shape guard, transaction, RTDB logging fixes) was correct for the real, separate problem it targeted, but none of them touched this fundamental operation, which is why the same fragment kept reappearing regardless. FIX [facSaveProfileFields() index.html ~14402]: read the whole array inside the transaction, clone it, modify only the matched element's fields in JS, write the WHOLE array back as one value (tx.update(ref, {visiting: newArr})) -- never a sub-path into an array again. Verified directly (not just node --check): ran the exact clone/modify logic against a simulated 15-row array, confirmed the output array is still 15 elements with only the target row changed. This is the actual fix -- prior 6 hotfixes tonight were all real and necessary for what they targeted, but this is the one that stops the recurring data loss. CODE_BUILD=1359.

## v1356 · 08-Sep-2026 IST

RE-ENABLE + FULL TRACE INSTRUMENTATION (direct request: 'to debug this issue i want its auto how to trace'). [facSaveProfileFields() index.html ~14337] rebuilt the Staff Directory mirror write as a Firestore TRANSACTION (db.runTransaction) instead of a plain get()-then-update() pair -- this directly targets the one remaining unexplained gap after 3 real corruptions and 4 fix attempts, all of which checked out clean in isolation every time: db.collection(...).get() and .update() are NOT atomic with each other, so nothing was stopping a DIFFERENT write (another tab, a concurrent login, an admin Staff Directory save) from landing in the exact gap between this function's own read and its own write. A transaction makes this structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely -- Firestore itself detects if the document changed between the transaction's read and write and automatically retries against fresh data, instead of silently completing a write based on data that's already stale. Also added full diagnostic logging on EVERY write attempt: console.log AND a new davan_pub/sdMirrorLog (RTDB) entry recording who triggered it, which fields, the exact matched row/index, the exact `updates` object sent, and (on skip) exactly why it was skipped -- if this corrupts a 4th time, the log will show precisely what happened instead of needing another live round-trip diagnostic. To read the trace log going forward: `rtdb.ref('davan_pub/sdMirrorLog').limitToLast(20).once('value').then(s => console.log(JSON.stringify(s.val(), null, 2)))` in the console shows the last 20 write attempts with full context. VERIFIED: all real inline script blocks node --check clean; also caught and fixed a structural leftover during this edit -- the previous emergency-disable version left orphaned dead code below the new block when first replaced, found by re-viewing the full function immediately after the edit rather than trusting the diff, and removed before this was called done. CRITICAL HOTFIX (direct report: "vising faculty data is not seen" -- Harsha correctly identified this session's OWN prior fix as the cause, and a raw sdData dump proved it: visiting:[] while nonteaching's real rows were fully intact, meaning the visiting DATA existed and this app's own code discarded it). FIX: [staffDirectoryRender() index.html ~15320] normalization now attempts Object.values() recovery FIRST when a section isn't a true array -- if the result looks like real row objects (has a .name field), it's used directly, with a console.warn confirming how many rows were recovered and zero data lost. Only falls back to a genuinely empty array if the value truly cannot be recovered (a string, a number, or an object that doesn't resemble faculty rows at all). VERIFIED the fix logic directly (not just node --check syntax): ran it against a simulated Firestore object-shape ({'0':{...},'1':{...}}) matching the exact quirk this fix targets, confirmed it correctly recovers all rows via Object.values() rather than discarding them. ## v1342 · 07-Sep-2026 IST

BUGFIX, BOTH index.html and student_portal.html (direct report with a real example: "Vijayalakshmi had her birthday in Jan, wishing anyone in Sep belated dont do good"). ROOT CAUSE: the belated-toast branch in both facMaybeShowBirthdayBanner() (index.html) and birthdayMaybeShowToast() (student_portal.html) checked only offset > 0 with NO upper bound. facBirthdayThisYearDate()/birthdayThisYearDate() always builds a birthday date in the CURRENT calendar year regardless of month, so a January birthday viewed in September produces offset ~240 (days past) — mathematically indistinguishable from someone who missed their birthday yesterday, so the unbounded check fired belated wishes for birthdays many months gone. This was actually MY OWN prior design decision, not a pre-existing bug: an earlier session explicitly specified "belated fires on ANY day after a missed birthday, however late" and that comment is still present in both files (now corrected) — that spec itself was wrong and is corrected here per direct instruction. FIX: both files' belated branch is now bounded to offset > 0 AND offset <= 30 — the top-of-function guard changed from "if (offset < -7) return" to "if (offset < -7 || offset > 30) return" in both files, and the belated branch condition changed from "else if (offset > 0)" to "else if (offset > 0 && offset <= 30)" in both. A birthday within the last 30 days still gets a belated wish (catches someone who missed a few weeks of logins); anything older simply gets nothing until next year's real countdown starts again at offset -7. ALSO (same report, separate ask): [facHoroscopeBadgeHtml() index.html ~14384] badge beside a faculty name now shows the actual DOB inline (e.g. "25 Dec 1980 · Capricorn"), not just the zodiac sign with DOB hidden in a hover-only tooltip — DOB was previously only reachable via title=, invisible until hover, per explicit instruction ("beside name u add zodic add dob also"). THREE STACKED BUGS FOUND AND FIXED, per direct admin report ("each login manager admin principal incharge should change the date then its showing shortage why its not showing to me raw and final both r no seen") + a UI confusion report ("why it says 7 when i have saved to 5"). THE REAL BUGS, three, stacked -- reading not-showing was never one single cause: (1) [iaeGetWindows() index.html ~35849] only ever tried Firestore then a PER-DEVICE localStorage cache -- never the RTDB public mirror. This file's own loadFirestoreData() (index.html ~10071) has documented for a while that Firestore is BLOCKED ENTIRELY for role in [manager, vp, principal] ("Firestore blocks on file:// origin") and already routes those roles' whole data load through _loadFromRTDB() instead -- but the IAE module (built later) called raw fsGet()/fsSet() everywhere, never accounting for that pre-existing, already-solved constraint, so on those logins the Firestore read threw every time and fell back to an empty per-device cache, silently showing "no cutoff set". FIX: added the same 3-tier Firestore-then-RTDB-public-mirror-then-localStorage fallback this file's own _fetchProfile() (index.html ~10044) already uses for this exact class of problem. FIX: RTDB mirror now always attempted independently of the Firestore outcome. (3) THE MAIN CAUSE, found by re-reading iaeGetSnapshot() line by line: once an exam LOCKS, the permanent result was read via ONE line -- `localStorage.getItem('davan_ia_snapshot_'+examTag)` -- pure per-BROWSER cache, never Firestore, never RTDB, even though _iaeLockSnapshot() genuinely does write the real snapshot to both. Only the ONE device that happened to perform the actual lock ever had it in ITS OWN localStorage -- every other login, on every other device, regardless of role, read that same line, got null, and silently showed no shortage data at all, forever, indistinguishable from "not locked yet". This is exactly why re-visiting from the admin's own device "made it show up" while other logins never saw it. FIX: new [IAE_SNAPSHOTS/iaeFetchLockedSnapshot() index.html ~36030] module-level cache populated via the same 3-tier Firestore/RTDB-mirror/localStorage pattern, wired into [iaeEnsureFresh() index.html ~38752] so every real render entry point fetches the genuine server-backed locked result on first use per session, on any device -- _iaeLockSnapshot() also seeds this cache in-memory immediately on the locking session itself, no round-trip needed there. ALSO: [login auto-publish index.html ~12218] removed the 4-role gate (admin/manager/vp/principal) entirely -- incharge is a classIncharge tag on a fulltime account, not a separate role, and was never covered by that list at all despite already having real view access to Final Shortage; iaeEnsureFresh() now fires on every login regardless of role since it is read-safe, idempotent, and independently throttled. CONFIRMED not a scrape-timing issue (admin explicitly checked two versions against the SAME Firebase) -- traced to [iarAutoApplyBatch() index.html ~35816, the +1/+2 rule auto-apply that runs on EVERY Final Shortage page-open]: it only ever wrote a TA rescue entry the FIRST time a subject was seen short, then never touched that entry again -- but the underlying raw CT/CA keeps moving on every scrape. So a TA=1 granted when raw was 71% silently went stale once new classes were scraped in and raw drifted to 68% (needs TA=2 now) or recovered to 76% on its own (rescue no longer needed, but stayed on record) -- and since each admin page-open runs this same auto-apply again, it kept newly clearing a few more students whose raw % had drifted past the line since their last visit, permanently writing that to davan_pub/ia_ta each time. This is why the total kept shrinking with zero manual edits: every single page-open was itself an irreversible write. FIX, per explicit admin decision (keep auto-applying but recompute against current data every time, do not freeze on first sight): [iarWindowedSubjects() index.html ~35701] now recomputes any appliedBy rule entry live against current raw CT/CA on every read -- recovered-on-its-own subjects display as genuinely clear, worsened ones display the correct current TA amount. [iarAutoApplyBatch() index.html ~35816] correspondingly now RECONCILES existing rule entries against current data (not just grants new ones): deletes a rule entry if raw recovered past threshold on its own, updates it if the required TA amount changed (e.g. +1 no longer enough, escalate to +2), leaves it untouched if still correct. An appliedBy manual entry (a deliberate admin override) is NEVER touched by any of this -- explicitly excluded in both functions, stays exactly as the admin set it until they change it themselves. If raw attendance has fallen so far that even +2 no longer clears a subject, the last-known TA is kept on record rather than silently dropped to 0, so a genuine worsening still surfaces as short rather than vanishing. VERIFIED: 5 isolated Node test cases against the real reconcile logic -- raw worsened past +1 (correctly escalates to +2), raw recovered on its own (correctly clears/deletes), manual override with raw worsening (correctly left untouched), still-short-same-TA-still-clears (correctly no-op, keeps this cheap on the common case), and raw fallen so far even +2 insufficient (correctly keeps last-known TA rather than dropping it) -- all 5 passed, confirmed the write-side reconcile and the display-side live-recompute agree with each other in every case. node --check clean on the containing script block. CODE_BUILD=1313.

## v1298 · 29-Aug-2026 IST

FIX, real bug reported live with a screenshot: in the new View-tab inline subject editor (v1297), clearing a subject in one cell (e.g. removing English from II BCA) did NOT make English reappear as an option in any OTHER cell dropdown for that same batch -- it stayed invisible everywhere until a full page reload, confirmed by admin as only happening in the new View editor, not in Create/Edit own picker. ROOT CAUSE: every cell dropdown option list is built ONCE, at initial table render (intBuildViewEditCell(), reading intGetSubjectsForBatch() usedElsewhere set) -- Create/Edit own picker never has this problem because intGetUsedSubjects() reads the LIVE DOM value of every other cell on every change; View cells instead read an in-memory data.slots snapshot, which intViewSaveSubject() WAS correctly keeping up to date after every save, but nothing ever told the other already-rendered dropdowns to recompute against that updated snapshot -- so a freed-up subject had the right underlying data the whole time, it just never reached the screen. FIX: [intViewSaveSubject() index.html ~48227] now re-renders the whole table (same intRenderTable() call the Edit-mode checkbox itself already uses) immediately after a confirmed save, so every cell option list is recomputed fresh from the current data and a freed subject reappears everywhere at once. Scroll position is captured before and restored after the rebuild, since a full table replace would otherwise jump the page back to the top on every single edit -- felt jarring correcting more than one cell in a row. VERIFIED: isolated Node harness, 3 test cases against the admin exact reported scenario (II BCA with English at one slot and Kannada/Hindi at another) -- confirms English is correctly excluded from a second cell dropdown while still assigned elsewhere, confirms English correctly REAPPEARS in that same second cell dropdown once cleared and the view is refreshed, and confirms the cleared cell ITSELF also correctly offers English again, not just other cells. CODE_BUILD=1298.

## v1285 · 27-Aug-2026 IST

CRITICAL FIX -- "Permanently Unavailable" (and every other duty_auto field: exceptions, maxOverrides, counts, days) was silently deleted from Firestore by the very next unrelated save, even though the click that set it wrote correctly. Traced live via the admin's own F12 wrapper diagnostic (intercepted dutyTogglePermanentException() at the real click, then re-read Firestore immediately after) -- confirmed the click itself DOES write ["Gnaneshwari. S. A"] into Firestore correctly, ruling out the toggle function and the Firestore rules as the cause. ROOT CAUSE, found by grepping every Firestore write to the internals collection: two separate .set() calls -- [intSave() index.html ~50249, the MAIN AUTOSAVE for every routine Internal edit] and [Calendar Sync date-remap index.html ~47676] -- both build a payload object listing only {meta, batches, slots, duties, batch_overrides} and call .set(payload) with NO merge option. Per Firestore's own documented behavior, a bare .set() REPLACES THE ENTIRE DOCUMENT with exactly the fields given -- any field not listed (duty_auto, and everything inside it) is deleted, not left alone. Since intSave() is the autosave path firing on nearly every timetable/meta edit, this meant: mark someone permanently unavailable -> write succeeds -> edit literally anything else on the same Internal -> next autosave silently erases duty_auto entirely, including permanentExceptions -- exactly the "I have to give it new one every new version" symptom reported, where "new version" meant a fresh admin edit/save cycle, not a new code deploy. FIX: both .set() calls now pass {merge:true} as the second argument, which changes Firestore's behavior to a partial write of only the listed top-level keys -- duty_auto (and anything else this function never touches) is now left completely untouched by either save path. [intSave() index.html ~50249] additionally had its post-await INT_DATA[docId] cache assignment changed from a full object replacement to a spread-merge against the existing cached object, since the in-memory cache had the identical field-dropping bug independent of Firestore -- without this, the UI would still show duty_auto as stale/missing until the next full reload even after the Firestore fix. VERIFIED: node --check clean on all real script blocks (block 9's </html>-inside-template-literal false positive is pre-existing, confirmed identical in the admin's own original uploaded file, not caused by this edit). A standalone Node harness simulating Firestore's actual documented .set() vs .set(payload,{merge:true}) semantics against a realistic existingDoc with duty_auto.permanentExceptions=["Gnaneshwari. S. A"] set, run against the OLD payload shape both ways, confirms: old behavior wipes duty_auto to undefined, new behavior preserves it byte-for-byte including permanentExceptions. ACTION: no data recovery possible for names already lost to a prior autosave wipe -- admin will need to re-mark any previously-set permanent exceptions once on this build; they will now actually persist through subsequent saves. CODE_BUILD=1285.

## v1253 · 25-Aug-2026 IST

STRUCTURAL FIX, per direct admin correction: EXAM DATES is just a flat list of time slots per day with NO inherent morning/afternoon meaning at all -- session is decided purely by which batch is picked into a cell, via that batch's own Morning/Afternoon setting in BATCHES. Every prior build in this chain (back through v1249) wrongly derived a row's session from its clock hour (hour<13=morning, else afternoon), which caused three concrete bugs the admin reported: an overflow row sorting above earlier rows on the same day (plain string sort put '01:15pm...' before '09:30am...'), and worse, a batch (III BCA) showing a WRONG subject that actually belonged to a different batch (I B.Com) at the same time slot -- a real data-corruption risk, not just a display glitch. ROOT CAUSE: INT_SLOT_BATCH_OVERRIDE keys are colIdx-based (date|time_label|colIdx), and colIdx was each batch's position within a PER-ROW, clock-hour-filtered subset of batches -- so the same real batch could land at different colIdx on different rows, meaning an override saved on one row could resolve to a completely different batch on another row after any grid refresh. FIX: removed the clock-hour session derivation everywhere it decided which batches belong to a row or how a slot's session gets saved -- [intBuildTimeEditor/intBuildTimeRow/intBuildSlotCell index.html ~48900-49075] now show every batch on the internal as a column on every row, in the exact same fixed order every time, so colIdx is now a stable pure function of a batch's position in the full batches array, identical between what is rendered and what gets read back -- eliminating the collision at its root rather than patching around it. [intCollectSlots/intRefreshAllDates index.html ~49820-49900+] now stamp each saved slot's session from the EFFECTIVE batch's own config, never from the row's clock time. [intMarkIgnored, intUpdateTimeSlot] updated to match the same stable-colIdx/config-session rule. [intRenderTable's getEffectiveBatch, index.html ~47964] fixed to resolve colIdx against the FULL batches array (matching the new write-side scheme) instead of the session-filtered display list, so the Timetable view reads back the correct override too. [renderSessionBlock, index.html ~47981] simplified -- a batch's slot always already carries its own correct session regardless of clock time, so the earlier 'overflow slot' special-casing was removed as unnecessary; its time-sort also switched from a plain string sort to a real chronological key (parses each label's leading HH:MMam/pm to real minutes) fixing the '01:15pm sorts before 09:30am' bug directly. Timetable row-visibility (a row shows if ANY batch in that session's table has a real slot there; batches with nothing at that exact time show a plain dash) was already correct and confirmed unchanged, per explicit admin confirmation of that exact display rule. Re-fill from Template [intRefillFromTemplate index.html ~49735] also rebuilt: matches now by each batch's OWN time-slot position that day (1st real slot, 2nd, etc.) rather than a shared clock-hour session bucket across all batches, since different batches can have entirely different slot counts/positions on the same date now; the now-meaningless intFixSessionSlots() repair call was removed from this path (its per-session clock-hour slot-count 'repair' no longer corresponds to anything real). Rebuild Grid from Batches+Dates (admin confirmed not used) was left untouched. Verified the full fix against the admin's exact reported shape (I B.Com/I BBA/III BCA all Morning, III BCA only 5 real subjects so genuinely nothing at 1:15pm, I B.Com+I BBA each with a real 1:15pm subject) via a standalone logic test covering intCollectSlots's save-time behavior AND the Timetable render's sort+lookup together: times now sort 9:30/11:30/1:15 in correct chronological order, III BCA correctly shows a dash (not a leaked subject) at 1:15pm, and I B.Com/I BBA show their own correct subjects -- matching the admin's confirmed expected output exactly. Because the override-key scheme changed, admin was informed and agreed that any batch-swap overrides saved under the old buggy scheme (e.g. the I B.Com/I BBA 1:15pm picks from before this fix) may need to be re-picked once; all other saved data is unaffected. ## v1235 · 24-Aug-2026 IST

BUG FIX: IA Window Settings' green "Saved" tick next to the cutoff date could show even when NOTHING was actually written to Firebase, per explicit admin request ("show green only if u get confirmation firbase it has saved"). ROOT CAUSE: [iaeSaveWindowsUI() index.html ~36988] tracked a single ok boolean that defaulted to true and was only ANDed with a real result for a field that actually differed from its saved value -- iaeEditCutoffDate() is only called per-field when that field's date genuinely changed, so clicking Save with BOTH dates already matching what was saved (or one changed and the other unchanged) still fell through to the unmodified true default and showed the green tick, despite zero Firebase writes having happened at all. The underlying write confirmation itself was already correct -- fsSet() genuinely awaits the real Firestore .set() call and only returns true if it didn't throw, no change needed there -- the gap was entirely in how the UI message decided which state to show when a field was never sent to Firebase in the first place. FIX: now tracks anyAttempted (was at least one field actually sent to iaeEditCutoffDate/fsSet) separately from allOk (did every attempted field genuinely succeed), giving three distinct outcomes instead of one collapsed boolean: gray "Nothing changed -- no save needed" when neither date differs from what is already saved (Save was clicked but there was truly nothing to confirm), green "Saved -- confirmed in Firebase" only when at least one field was actually written AND every attempted field's fsSet() call genuinely returned true, red "Save failed or cancelled" if anything attempted failed (network/permission error) or the admin cancelled the already-locked confirm dialog. Verified all 5 real scenarios in isolation (Node) before wiring in: nothing changed correctly shows gray not green; a genuine successful save shows green; a failed write shows red; a mixed result (IA1 saves, IA2 fails) correctly shows red rather than the old logic's silent pass; cancelling the locked-exam confirm dialog correctly shows red. CODE_BUILD=1235.

## v1234 · 24-Aug-2026 IST

BUG FIX: IA1/IA2 cutoff date could appear wrong or reset after a version update, per direct admin report ("every time new version update to github cutoff date has to be update why so it's database driven process why it go off"). ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading the actual code rather than guessing: [iaeGetWindows() index.html ~34921] -- the single function every IA Eligibility surface calls to read the cutoff date -- read ONLY localStorage, never Firestore, despite app_data/ia_windows being the real saved value and the actual source of truth. This is not a GitHub/version-number issue at all -- a version update just happens to force a fresh page load, and whatever was sitting in that browser's local cache at that moment (which could be stale, from a different device, or from before the admin's last edit) is what got shown, with nothing ever re-checking the real database value. FIX: iaeGetWindows() is now async and fetches app_data/ia_windows from Firestore FIRST on every call, rewriting the local cache with whatever Firestore returns so the two can never drift apart again; falls back to the local cache only if the Firestore read itself genuinely fails (offline, permission error), never as the default path. All 10 real call sites updated to await it -- every one was already inside an async function (iaeEditCutoffDate, _iaeLockSnapshot, iaeCheckAndAutoLock, iafRender, ialRender, iaePublishLiveStatus, iaeRender, iaeRenderSettings, iaeSaveWindowsUI, iaedRender), so no new async boundaries were needed except iaeRenderSettings()/iaeToggleSettings() themselves, which were synchronous and are now async (safe as onclick handlers, verified their one call site is a plain onclick which async functions work fine as). One exception: [iaeGetSnapshot() index.html ~35074] is called from several render paths that are not all async, so rather than force async through the whole call chain it now reads the module-level IAE_WINDOWS cache directly (synchronous) instead of calling iaeGetWindows() itself -- safe because every real call site already runs iaeEnsureFresh() (which awaits a fresh iaeGetWindows() fetch) before reaching iaeGetSnapshot(), so IAE_WINDOWS is guaranteed current by the time this reads it. Verified the core fetch-then-fallback logic in isolation (Node, 3 scenarios: Firestore returns fresh data and correctly overrides a stale local cache and rewrites it; Firestore read throws and correctly falls back to the cache instead of crashing; Firestore returns null with no cache and returns a safe default without crashing) before wiring in, plus confirmed via Node's real parser that the full main script still loads with zero syntax errors after the async conversion across all 10 call sites. CODE_BUILD=1234.

## v1204 · 23-Aug-2026 IST

FIX: Final Shortage tab (and the underlying iaeStudentShortage()/iaeWindowedSubjects() calls shared by IA Raw + IA Ledger too) reported still blank even after v1203's RTDB key fix, on a real dataset. Investigated with actual complexity analysis rather than another guess-and-patch: TWO real performance bugs found, both O(n^2)-class, neither a crash (nothing throws, which is why the on-screen red error from v1201 never fired -- the code was working, just doing a catastrophic amount of redundant work before ever finishing a render). BUG 1 -- [iaeGetSnapshot() index.html ~34724, in the not-yet-locked/live branch] called _iaeBuildLiveData() -- which loops over EVERY student in the college -- on every single invocation, and this function is called ONCE PER STUDENT inside iafRender()'s own per-student loop. For N students that is N full re-loops of all N students = O(N^2): confirmed by simulation at N=500 this is 250,000 redundant student-iterations for one single tab render, a ~250x blowup versus the ~1,000 operations the same render actually needs. FIX: added a short in-memory cache (_iaeLiveSnapshotCache, 2-second TTL) so the live snapshot is built AT MOST once per TTL window instead of once per lookup -- TTL chosen over pure event-based invalidation because allStudents is reassigned at several call sites across this file (initial load, refresh, scope changes) and manually finding+invalidating at every one of them risks missing a future site, the same "remember to do X everywhere" failure mode that caused the v1202 RTDB bug; a 2s TTL is invisible to a human but eliminates the redundant rebuilds within one render pass. Explicit invalidation (_iaeInvalidateLiveCache(), called from iaeSaveWindows()) still runs as a fast-path on top of the TTL for changes known to affect it (lock-state transitions). BUG 2 -- [iafRender() index.html ~35349, previously] called iarAutoApplyForStudent() once per flagged student, and THAT function performed its own full Firestore+RTDB save via iarSaveTA() for each one individually, awaited sequentially -- meaning up to one full network round-trip PER FLAGGED STUDENT had to complete, in order, before the tab could finish rendering; on any real flagged-student count (dozens is plausible for a whole institution) this alone could take the tab from instant to effectively frozen. FIX: new [iarAutoApplyBatch() index.html ~35010] computes every student's rule-clearance entirely in memory first, then performs exactly ONE iarSaveTA() write covering all of them -- collapsing up to hundreds of sequential saves into one. iarAutoApplyForStudent() (the single-student version) is kept for any future call site that genuinely only touches one student, where batching overhead isn't worth it -- iafRender() itself now calls the batch version exclusively. Both fixes verified numerically (complexity simulation for bug 1) and by code-path tracing (bug 2) rather than assumed. CODE_BUILD=1204.

## v1203 · 23-Aug-2026 IST

CORE FIX (admin explicitly asked why v1202 patched one call site instead of the actual root cause -- correct call, done here): the ".#$/[]" illegal-RTDB-key problem is not a property of any one feature's data shape, it is a property of RTDB itself -- and this exact bug class has now hit this codebase TWICE via two unrelated call sites months apart (faculty names with periods; then v1202's IA subject names with slashes), each individually patched with a manual per-field encoder. Manually remembering to sanitize keys at each of the ~196 rtdb.ref(...).set(...) call sites across this file is exactly how it slipped through a second time -- that discipline-based approach was the actual root cause, not any single missing encode call. REAL FIX: new [_rtdbDeepSanitizeKeys() index.html ~30380] recursively walks ANY value -- arrays, nested objects, any depth -- and runs every OBJECT KEY (never values; "Indian Constitution (CVC) 40/10" stored as a plain string value is completely fine in RTDB, only path-segment keys are restricted) through the existing _rtdbSafeKey() helper automatically. New [rtdbSafeSet(path, value) index.html ~30398] is a drop-in replacement for rtdb.ref(path).set(value) with the identical signature and return type (a Promise) that makes this safety automatic rather than something a future call site has to remember. MIGRATED the entire IA module (the one that just broke) to it as the first real adopter: iaeSaveWindows, _iaeLockSnapshot, iaeSavePermissions, iarSaveTA, iarAppendLog -- all 6 davan_pub/ia_* RTDB writes now go through rtdbSafeSet(), and v1202's one-off _iarEncodeTAMapForFirebase() (a manual, IA-module-specific version of exactly this same idea) was deleted and replaced by the generic core version so there is only ONE sanitizer in this codebase, not two doing the same job differently. THE OTHER ~190 rtdb.ref(...).set() call sites across the rest of this file are NOT yet migrated -- a single mass find-replace across the whole file was deliberately avoided in this edit since blindly touching ~190 call sites at once (many in features unrelated to what was being tested, e.g. duty allocation, live class board, meter tracker) risks introducing an unrelated regression far larger than the bug being fixed; the safer path is migrating each area to rtdbSafeSet() as it is next touched for any other reason, which this changelog entry documents as the now-standard pattern new code should follow. Verified the sanitizer against the exact reported string plus a deliberately adversarial case combining all 5 illegal characters at multiple nesting depths, plus confirmed array-valued fields (e.g. the edit log's subject:"..." stored inside a list) pass through completely untouched since only object KEYS are ever rewritten, never values. CODE_BUILD=1203.

## v1202 · 23-Aug-2026 IST

FIX (real root cause, not another band-aid): the v1201 error-visibility fix correctly surfaced the ACTUAL bug -- "set failed: value argument contains an invalid key (Indian Constitution (CVC) 40/10)". ROOT CAUSE: [iarSaveTA() index.html ~34845, previously] wrote the TA storage object DIRECTLY to Firebase using real subject names as nested object keys -- e.g. davan_pub.ia_ta.IA1.<urn>."Indian Constitution (CVC) 40/10" -- and Firebase (both RTDB and, in practice, Firestore nested maps) rejects keys containing ".", "#", "$", "/", "[", "]". This is the EXACT SAME bug class already fixed once before in this codebase for faculty names containing periods (see _rtdbSafeKey()/_rtdbUnsafeKey(), index.html:30366) -- that existing helper was not reused when the IA Rules Engine (v1199) was built, which is the actual miss. FIX: new [_iarEncodeTAMapForFirebase() index.html ~34845] runs every urn AND subject key in the TA map through the existing _rtdbSafeKey() helper (not a new encoding scheme -- reusing the one already proven in this file) at the single point [iarSaveTA()] where data leaves the app for Firestore/RTDB. Every other function in the module (iarGetTA, iarSetTA, iarAutoApplyForStudent, iarBulkRevert, iarRuleForSubject, all UI renderers) continues to read/write REAL, human-readable subject names exactly as before -- the encode/decode boundary is isolated to the one write call, so no caller above it needed to change. localStorage was never affected (JSON.stringify has no key restrictions), so this bug only manifested on an actual Firebase save attempt, which is why it surfaced as the specific runtime error reported rather than a syntax or logic failure. Verified by reproducing the exact reported subject string "Indian Constitution (CVC) 40/10" through the new encoder in isolation -- confirmed zero illegal characters remain in the resulting key. Also audited every other IA-module storage function (iaeGetPermissions/iaeSavePermissions, iarGetLog/iarAppendLog, _iaeBuildLiveData/_iaeLockSnapshot) for the same pattern -- all of them store subject names as ARRAY VALUES or plain object FIELD VALUES, never as object KEYS, so none of them share this vulnerability; only the TA map used subject-as-key, and only that one write path needed the fix. SUPERSEDED by v1203, which replaced the one-off _iarEncodeTAMapForFirebase() from this entry with a generic, codebase-wide fix. CODE_BUILD=1202.

## v1201 · 23-Aug-2026 IST

FIX: Final Shortage tab (and IA Raw / IA Ledger) showed a completely BLANK content area instead of any output at all -- admin screenshot confirmed: tab correctly highlighted active, search box rendered, but nothing below it, not even an empty-state message. ROOT CAUSE: [intSwitchTab() index.html ~47201-47203] called iaeRender()/iafRender()/ialRender() as bare fire-and-forget statements -- all three are async functions, and a bare async call with no .catch() means any thrown error inside them (or inside anything they await, e.g. iaeEnsureFresh()->iaeCheckAndAutoLock()) becomes an UNHANDLED PROMISE REJECTION: it logs to console but the calling code never runs its own error-recovery path, so whatever partial DOM state existed before the throw (in this case, an untouched empty <div id="iaf-output">) is what stays on screen forever -- no error message, no fallback text, just silence. FIX: all three call sites now chain .catch(e => ...) that logs the real error to console AND writes a visible red "⚠ Failed to load: <message>" into the relevant output div, so a future failure is diagnosable on-screen instead of presenting as an unexplained blank panel. Also added the same .catch() to the two iaeEnsureFresh() fire-and-forget calls in sitInit()/attInit() (index.html ~51103, ~54096) for the identical reason, marked non-fatal since those two call sites intentionally do not block on the result. This does not by itself explain what the ORIGINAL thrown error was (most likely: no IA1 cutoff date has been set yet on this install, which is a normal/expected state that iafRender() already has a proper messaged branch for -- the blank screen was masking that message, not a sign the branch is broken) -- if a genuine error is still occurring under real data, the new on-screen red text will now say exactly what it is. CODE_BUILD=1201.

## v1200 · 23-Aug-2026 IST

FIX: version badge flashed a WRONG old version number on every fast refresh before settling on the real one -- admin caught this on the topbar 9+ notification badge area. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: two separate hardcoded stale placeholder strings baked directly into the static HTML, painted by the browser immediately on parse, well before this file's single blocking (no defer/async) script tag reaches the JS lines that overwrite them with the real CODE_BUILD/BUILD_TIMESTAMP values -- (1) [markup index.html:1480] #topbar-version literally shipped "HTML: v1044 -- Last Updated: 26-Jul-2026 00:20 IST" hardcoded in the span's own text content, only corrected once syncDataTimestampUI() runs on the DOMContentLoaded listener [index.html ~25557] -- on a fast reload the v1044 text is genuinely on-screen and visible for that gap, not a rendering artifact or timing illusion. (2) [markup index.html:24690] #footer-version-num had the identical bug, hardcoded to "1139". Both are LEFTOVER values from whatever CODE_BUILD happened to be true whenever that markup was last hand-edited -- every subsequent version bump since then updated the constant but never touched these two literal HTML strings, so they silently drifted further out of date with every release while still being the very first thing painted on screen. FIX: both spans now ship EMPTY (index.html:1480, index.html:24690) -- there is no wrong number to flash because there is no hardcoded number at all; the true value appears exactly once, when JS actually knows what it is, instead of appearing twice (wrong then right). Investigated moving the fill earlier than DOMContentLoaded (e.g. inline immediately after the span) but confirmed CODE_BUILD/BUILD_TIMESTAMP/syncDataTimestampUI() aren't defined until much later in this same script (~line 14637 and ~25537 respectively, this being one large top-to-bottom parsed <script> block, not deferred) -- calling them any earlier is not possible without restructuring script load order, which is out of scope for this fix; DOMContentLoaded is already the earliest point those functions exist, so the remaining brief blank gap before the real number appears is an honest reflection of normal parse time, not a second bug. CODE_BUILD=1200.

## v1195 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

REAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND for the calendar->Internal sync date mismatch, via admin's own console output (a genuine debugging breakthrough -- exact oldDatesSet/sortedNew values were captured and compared against the calendar table's displayed 10-12 Sep dates). Confirmed: NO duplicate calendar event, cache was already fixed in v1194, dropdown was correctly set to '1st Internal' -- yet sortedNew computed as 09/10/11 Sep instead of 10/11/12 Sep, a consistent ONE-DAY-EARLY shift on every date. Reproduced exactly via Node in Asia/Kolkata timezone: [calSaveEvent() index.html ~54022]'s date-range builder used `new Date(from+'T00:00:00').toISOString().slice(0,10)` -- toISOString() converts to UTC, and in IST (UTC+5:30) midnight local time is 18:30 the PREVIOUS day in UTC, so every date in the loop came out exactly one day too early. This is the same class of bug as the already-documented stuParseCalDate() zero-holidays fix (invalid/UTC-unsafe Date string handling) but in a different function that was never covered by that earlier fix. FIX: new local _fmtLocalISO(d) helper builds the date string from the Date object's own local getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate() fields, never via toISOString()/UTC conversion -- verified via Node simulation in Asia/Kolkata timezone that From=10 Sep/To=12 Sep now correctly produces [2026-09-10, 2026-09-11, 2026-09-12], not the previous off-by-one result. Also audited intSyncFromCalendar() itself for the same UTC-conversion pattern -- confirmed clean, no toISOString() calls exist there, so this was the single isolated source of the bug, not a second occurrence. CODE_BUILD=1195.

Also added console.log of the actual oldDatesSet/sortedNew being compared, both on the no-op and the sync-fires paths, so any future mismatch is immediately diagnosable via the browser console/Eruda instead of requiring another round of screenshots. ## v1183 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

SITTING PRINT — 12 PAGES INSTEAD OF 6, PORTRAIT-SHAPED PREVIEW DESPITE @page LANDSCAPE. Admin uploaded a second print-dialog screenshot: Scale was correctly at Default this time, but the job showed 12 pages for 6 rooms (each room spilling onto 2 pages) and the preview pane itself was narrow/tall — i.e. genuinely portrait-shaped — despite v1182's @page{size:A4 landscape} rule. Root cause: .page was hardcoded to width:297mm (the landscape content width) regardless of what the actual paper turned out to be. Since the preview confirms the real paper here IS portrait A4 (210mm wide) — meaning @page's landscape hint is evidently not being honored reliably in this browser/print-preview path — a 297mm-wide .page no longer fits a 210mm-wide page at all, forcing the print engine to spill the overflow onto a second page per room. FIX: [sitBuildPrintHtml() index.html] .page now sizes off the VIEWPORT (width:100vw;height:100vh) instead of a hardcoded mm value, with overflow:hidden — the print-preview viewport already reflects whatever the real selected paper shape turns out to be (portrait or landscape), so the div can never again be wider than the actual page, regardless of whether the @page orientation hint is honored. @page{size:A4 landscape} itself is kept as a hint for browsers/flows that do respect it (giving the intended wide layout for the seat-grid table), but now even if it's ignored and the real paper is portrait, content reflows to fit that shape instead of overflowing onto extra pages. table-layout:fixed (set in v1181) already ignores cell min-width under this layout mode, so no additional horizontal-overflow risk was introduced by staying on a narrower portrait page. CODE_BUILD=1183.

## v1182 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

SITTING PRINT — SCALE 72% IN BROWSER DIALOG IS WHY IT LOOKS SMALL. Admin uploaded a screenshot of Chrome's print dialog confirming the actual cause of the still-small print: Scale was manually set to Custom 72%, shrinking the whole page regardless of anything in the sheet's own CSS — this cannot be fixed from inside the document, since Scale lives entirely in the browser's print UI, outside any @page or element CSS's reach. While tracing this, found and fixed a real (if separate) CSS bug: [sitBuildPrintHtml() index.html] had size:landscape written on .page INSIDE an @media print block — size is only a valid property on the @page at-rule itself, never on a regular element selector, so this was silently a no-op the whole time and landscape orientation only ever came from whatever the user picked in the print dialog's own Layout dropdown, with zero hint from the document. Replaced with a genuine @page{size:A4 landscape;margin:0} rule so the print preview defaults to the correct page size/orientation on its own, independent of what Layout the user has selected — margin left at 0 since .page's own 10mm padding already provides the visual margin. CODE_BUILD=1182.

## v1187 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

(1) REAL ROOT CAUSE OF THE RTDB MIRROR FAILURE, finally: the v1186 error-surfacing fix worked exactly as intended and immediately showed the actual error -- "invalid key (Dr. Shilpa R Y) in property davan_pub.internals_current.duty_auto.counts. Keys must be non-empty strings and cannot contain ., #, $, /, [, or ]". duty_auto.counts is a plain object KEYED BY RAW FACULTY NAME (counts[chosen.name]++ in the allocator) and gets written verbatim into RTDB -- Firebase RTDB forbids those characters in KEY names specifically (values are unrestricted), and "Dr. Shilpa R Y" has a period. This is the exact same bug class already found and fixed twice before for different fields -- _rtdbSafeKey()/_rtdbUnsafeKey() (v994, class_notes) and the old _sanitizeRtdbKeys() (v875/877, results subject keys) -- just never applied to duty_auto since that field did not exist yet when those fixes shipped. FIX: new _dutyAutoToRtdbSafe()/_dutyAutoFromRtdbSafe() [index.html ~49912] reuse the proven _rtdbSafeKey/_rtdbUnsafeKey encode-decode pair, applied ONLY to the counts sub-object (the one actual keyed-by-name field -- days/exceptions/permanentExceptions all store names as ARRAY VALUES or nested VALUES, never as object keys, so they need no encoding) and ONLY at the RTDB read/write boundary -- Firestore, INT_DATA, DUTY_AUTO, and the allocator itself keep using raw names untouched throughout, since Firestore has no such restriction and every existing counts[name] lookup across the allocator/admin-card/faculty-tab/widget-sync is proven correct against raw names today. Wired into all 6 RTDB write sites that include duty_auto (intLoadList auto-mirror, intSave x3, intSetCurrent, dutyAllocateForInternal) and the 2 faculty-facing RTDB read sites that cache the raw blob into INT_DATA (intLoadList's faculty branch, intDutyLoad's fallback) -- the widget-sync read at index.html ~10521 needed no change since it only ever reads .days (values), never .counts. (2) PULL-TO-REFRESH LANDING PAGE: per explicit request ("whichever tab I am working on at last"), new _navSaveState()/_navRestoreState() [index.html, switchPanel() section] persist the active sidebar panel to localStorage on every switchPanel() call, plus the Internal Timetable panel's own sub-tab via a matching hook in intSwitchTab() (the specific case reported -- other multi-tab panels are not yet wired, can be extended the same way later if needed). Restored once per login/reload from onLoginSuccess(), immediately after the existing role-based startPanel routing, so a saved state overrides the default landing panel when present and valid for the current role, but safely falls through to the normal default if the saved panel does not exist or is not visible for this session's role (e.g. device previously used for a different login). A pull-to-refresh or hard reload now returns to the exact panel+tab last open instead of always resetting to the role's default dashboard. CODE_BUILD=1187.

## v1191 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

PULL-TO-REFRESH: ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, verified via isolated Node simulation of the real call sequence (not guessed). [_navRestoreState() index.html ~14421, called from onLoginSuccess() ~11672] was reading localStorage AFTER switchPanel(startPanel) had already run on the line directly above it -- and switchPanel() [index.html ~14355] unconditionally calls _navSaveState({panel:name}) on EVERY call, including that startPanel one. So the very act of landing on the roles default panel overwrote the saved .panel field with that same default BEFORE _navRestoreState() ever got to read it back -- saved.panel was structurally guaranteed to always equal startPanel by the time it was checked, meaning the restore branch could never fire regardless of the visibility guard, timing fixes, or intInit() changes shipped in v1187/v1188/v1189, none of which touched this actual bug. CONFIRMED via a Node simulation reproducing the exact sequence (session 1: navigate to internals/autoduty and save; session 2/reload: compute startPanel, call switchPanel(startPanel), then call the old restore logic) -- the old code provably always read back the just-set default, never the real saved panel; the same simulation with the fix applied correctly restores to the genuine previous panel. FIX: onLoginSuccess() now captures a snapshot of localStorage BEFORE calling switchPanel(startPanel) at all, and passes that snapshot directly into _navRestoreState(preCapturedSnapshot) as a parameter instead of letting the function re-read localStorage itself (which by then would be corrupted) -- falls back to a fresh read only if ever called with no argument, for safety. Also added console.log tracing at every layer of the chain (onLoginSuccess entry, the pre-switchPanel snapshot capture, every switchPanel call showing what its saving, and every branch inside _navRestoreState) per explicit admin request for Eruda-visible debug output, so if anything still does not work as expected the exact failure point is now directly visible in the mobile console instead of requiring another round of blind guessing. CODE_BUILD=1191.

(2) .page changed to display:flex;flex-direction:column and table given flex:1, so the table (and its rows) actually grow to fill whatever vertical space remains after the header/legend above it, instead of collapsing to its natural content height and leaving the remainder of the page empty. ## v1179 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

ATTENDANCE PDF — FIT TO A4, EXPLICITLY. v1178's rebuild set the page format to real A4 (format:'a4') but never actually constrained the TABLE to that page's usable width — autoTable was left to size the subject columns itself (content-based) on top of fixed-mm widths for the first 4 columns, so the combined width could still exceed the page for a class with several subjects, silently overflowing past the right margin or onto extra pages: the page was A4, the table wasn't. FIX: [attDownloadPDF()] now computes the exact usable width (page width minus both margins), reserves a fixed budget for the 4 non-subject columns (#, Photo, URN, Name), and divides whatever's left EQUALLY across however many subject columns exist — every column gets an explicit columnStyles.cellWidth (not just the first 4), plus tableWidth set to that exact usable width, so autoTable is never left to size anything on its own. Font size also steps down automatically (7.5pt → 6pt body, 7pt → 5.5pt header) once there are more than 6 subjects, since a fixed page width with more columns means less room per column and unshrunk text would start clipping inside cells that are now correctly narrow instead of correctly overflowing. Also fixed a related gap: the footer (Total Students + signature block) was written at a fixed offset below the table with no check against the page's actual height — for a long student list the table could run to the bottom of the page and the footer would print past the printable area; now checks remaining space and starts a fresh page for the footer if there isn't enough room, using pdf.internal.pageSize.getHeight() rather than assuming a fixed height. Net effect: the exported sheet is now genuinely constrained to A4's real usable area on every side (width via column budget, height via footer page-break), regardless of subject count or student count. CODE_BUILD=1179.
