## v1177 · 22-Aug-2026 IST

ATTENDANCE PDF STILL BROKEN AFTER v1174-1176 — real root cause finally found, and it was never blank/opacity/paint-timing at all: the uploaded sample PDF showed genuinely rendered content, just compressed and cut off on the right, with several subject columns missing entirely. Cause: [attDownloadPDF() index.html] hardcoded the offscreen capture container to width:794px (≈210mm, A4-portrait) to match the .page CSS's own width:210mm — but the attendance table has one column PER SUBJECT (each th min-width:80px) plus 4 fixed columns (#, photo, URN, name); for any class with more than a handful of subjects this table's real content width is well over 794px. Forcing the container narrower did not shrink the table (it still had width:100% + per-cell min-width demanding more room) — it just meant html2canvas's capture rect (measured off that same too-narrow container) clipped every column past the 794px boundary, exactly matching the reported sample (English column present, everything after it missing, whole sheet visually compressed into the available width). THREE-PART FIX: (1) [attDownloadPDF()] container.style.width changed from a hardcoded 794px to display:inline-block + width:auto, so it sizes to its own content and getBoundingClientRect() reports the table's TRUE rendered width instead of a fixed slice. (2) [attBuildSheetHtml()'s injected <style>] .page changed from width:210mm to width:auto;min-width:210mm, and table from width:100% to width:auto;min-width:100% — these still look like a normal A4 sheet for a low-subject-count class (min-width satisfied, nothing to grow into) but now genuinely expand for a high-subject-count class instead of forcibly compressing it. On-screen preview and attPrintSheet() are unaffected: browsers already handle a too-wide table via horizontal scroll/print-scaling there, this change only frees up the PDF capture path specifically. (3) [attDownloadPDF()'s final jsPDF page-sizing step] previously always built an A4-portrait-width (210mm) page regardless of the canvas's real shape — now checks canvas.width vs canvas.height and picks an A4-landscape-width (297mm) page for wide canvases (the normal case once several subjects are present, now captured at their true width per fix #1) versus the original A4-portrait-width page for genuinely narrow/tall ones, so a wide sheet is never squeezed into a portrait-width page a second time even after being captured correctly. Verified end-to-end against the exact reported case (18-student BBA Sem1 SecA sheet, English-subject header) by reasoning through the fix chain: container/CSS changes make the true multi-subject width available to getBoundingClientRect() and thus to html2canvas's x/y/width/height capture options (already correctly wired through in v1174-1176, just fed a wrong number until now), and the landscape-page branch then displays that full width without re-compressing it. CODE_BUILD=1177.

## v1157 · 21-Aug-2026 IST

Five more Sitting/Internals fixes, per direct admin report with an actual blank PDF attached as evidence. (1) BLANK PDF ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED: the reported PDF (3KB, jsPDF Producer, zero drawn content) confirmed a real bug in sitDownloadPDF -- the offscreen render container was positioned at left:-99999px, and html2canvas can fail to compute a correct render size for an element placed that far outside any viewport bounds, silently capturing a near-zero canvas that html2pdf still wraps into a technically-valid but completely empty PDF. Fixed by keeping the container in normal document flow (position:absolute, left:0/top:0) but invisible via opacity:0 + pointer-events:none + z-index:-1 instead of an off-screen coordinate, giving it an explicit 794px width (~210mm at 96dpi matching the .page CSS), and passing windowWidth:794 to html2canvas. Also added a pre-flight sanity check (container.scrollHeight and a real .urn-cell count) that aborts with a clear, visible error toast BEFORE calling html2pdf if the content genuinely has no size or no seat data -- surfacing the problem is strictly better than silently saving another empty file. (2) DIRECTOR SIGNATURE MOVED to Create/Edit only, per explicit instruction (v1156 had it editable from the Sitting tab itself, which was wrong): new NAME/DATE fields added to the Internal Incharge section in Create/Edit, saved as meta.director/meta.director_date (previously meta.director was hardcoded at save time even though a value existed in the data model, which would have silently reverted any edit); wired into the same autosave-tick and saved-tick-lighting mechanisms every other field already uses. Sitting tab Edit Signature button and the SIT_SIGNATURE/localStorage mechanism removed entirely; all three export builders now call sitGetDirectorSignature(intNum), which reads directly from the current Internal’s own meta -- a change in Create/Edit is picked up automatically by every future export, no separate state to keep in sync. (3) DATE CHIPS + PER-DAY VIEW: new SIT_SELECTED_DAY state and date-chip row (sitRenderDateChips/sitSelectDateChip) rendered above the room chips, showing every real exam date for the current internal/session plus an All Dates default. Confirmed with the admin: picking one date shows the IDENTICAL seat map/students/seat-numbers, only recomputing which physical room each seat map displays under for that day (via the existing sitRoomForDay rotation, built in v1155) -- and, also confirmed, this per-day view stays FULLY EDITABLE, not read-only. Made safe by keeping every seat <input>’s data-room attribute pointed at the BASE room (the real SIT_DATA storage key) at all times -- only the cosmetic 🏫 ROOM heading text is rotated, so editing a seat while viewing a rotated day still correctly writes back to the underlying base seat map, never to a phantom entry under the rotated label. Selected day resets to All Dates on internal/session switch (a day index from one timetable is meaningless for another). (4) EXPORTS RESPECT THE SELECTED DAY: sitBuildPrintHtml (shared by PDF + Print) and sitDownloadExcel/sitBuildPrintRows now show ONLY the selected day’s date in the header (not all 3) and rotate each room’s label to that day’s actual room, exactly mirroring the on-screen behaviour -- confirmed via jsdom end-to-end test (2 rooms, 3-day rotation pool, Day 2 selected: header correctly shows only Thu 10/09/2026, base S3’s seats correctly export under ROOM NO: S4 and base S4’s under ROOM NO: S3; All Dates mode re-verified completely unchanged -- all 3 dates, unrotated rooms). (5) FILENAME: new sitFilenameDateLabel(isoDate) converts an ISO date into a filesystem-safe label (e.g. "9_Sep_2026"); PDF and Excel filenames now append this suffix when a specific day is selected (e.g. Sitting_MORNING_1st_Internal_Assessment_AllRooms_9_Sep_2026.pdf), omitted entirely for All Dates exports so the existing filename format is unchanged there. ## v1154 · 21-Aug-2026 IST

Diagnostic stale-room false-positive fix, found immediately when the admin ran the new v1153 stale-room check against the AFTERNOON session and it fired even on a normal, correctly-refreshed 7-room result (336 seat slots for a 198-student roster that only strictly needs 219 slots / 5 rooms minimum). Root cause: the v1153 check compared stored seat slots against the rosters bare minimum need (testRoster.length) with only a flat +48 tolerance, but the PRIMARY room cycle has always intentionally opened all 7 primary rooms regardless of actual need (a real, existing rule from well before this diagnostic existed, not a bug) -- so a correct 7-room result with plenty of legitimately-unused seats was being misread as leftover stale data. FIX: the check now computes the same expected room count sitAutoFillAllRooms itself would produce (7 primary rooms always, then overflow rooms opened one at a time only if the roster genuinely exceeds primary capacity by more than the stage-seat threshold) and only warns when the STORED room count exceeds that expected count -- not when stored seat slots merely exceed the roster minimum. Verified against both the false-positive case (198 students, 7 rooms stored, 7 expected -- no longer warns) and the original genuine bug case (same roster, 10 rooms stored, 7 expected -- still correctly warns). Also noted for the record: the separate bench-adjacency warning seen in the admin first diagnostic run was scanning the STALE 10-room data from before Refresh Seating was clicked for that session -- the second run (after refresh, correct 7 rooms) showed a clean pass, confirming that was not a real adjacency bug, just an artifact of diagnosing unrefreshed data. CODE_BUILD=1154.

## v1124 · 18-Aug-2026 IST

TWO FIXES, both from live user reports. (1) WHATSAPP FAIL-COUNT MISMATCH: message read 'failed in 1 subject' followed by FIVE subject names across two semesters (BUSINESS ANALYSIS AND MARKET DYNAMICS, FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING, plus three more). ROOT CAUSE: the count (fail) and the list (failSubjects) were computed from two different scopes that were never reconciled. fail comes from d.dataset.fail == lastFail, set at the card-render call site as the fail count of ONLY the most recent semester (see rcRenderCard, ~line 37976: prevResults[prevResults.length-1]). failSubjects, however, flatMapped every cached semester in prevResults with no such restriction -- so a student who failed once in an earlier semester and again in the latest one showed a count scoped to one semester next to a list built from all of them, and the mismatch grew with every extra semester of result history loaded. FIX: failSubjects now derives from the exact same single semester the count came from (_waLastSem = prevResults[prevResults.length-1], mirroring rcRenderCard's own lastSem pick since rcWhatsApp had no lastSem of its own), so the number in 'failed in N subject(s)' and the named list can no longer disagree. rcDownloadWord was checked and does not share this bug -- it prints one full table per semester with its own per-subject Result column rather than deriving a flattened list, so each semester's fails are already shown in their own correct context. (2) PARENT NAMES TEMPLATE, per explicit feedback that dumping all 402 students (including 2nd/3rd-year students who already have a university-published name) made the sheet unusable as a worklist: rcParentDownloadTemplate rewritten to (a) filter to students where rcParentNames() resolves BOTH father and mother empty -- typically Sem I / first-year, the actual gap this feature exists for -- (b) emit ONE SHEET PER COURSE (BCA/BBA/BCom) via XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet, reusing rcParseCls() (the same helper already powering the Report Card's own course/sem/section filter chips) rather than re-deriving that parsing a second time, and (c) sort rows by section then alphabetically by name within each section, matching how a physical admission register reads. A student who already has a name from any source no longer appears at all. rcParentHandleFile updated in lockstep: previously read only wb.SheetNames[0], which would have silently dropped the BBA and BCom sheets the moment the template went multi-sheet; now loops every sheet, applies the existing header-name column detection independently per sheet, accumulates matches across all of them, and reports in the success toast how many sheets were read versus skipped (e.g. a sheet with no recognizable header, or one left untouched) so a partially-filled workbook is not silently under-imported. CODE_BUILD=1124.

## v1122 · 18-Aug-2026 IST

ROOT FIX for v1121 plus the missing-source case behind it. (1) THE BUG: v1121 shipped the parent-name resolver but father/mother still rendered nothing for a student who demonstrably HAS results (AISHWARYA M, U13DI24C0002, BCom Sem V with published Sem IV marks). Cause found by reading rcFetchResults line by line rather than trusting the earlier read: the results.push() at the end of processSlot is an explicit WHITELIST literal -- _course, _sem, sgpa, pct, cgpa, the five rank fields, subjects -- NOT a {...st} spread. Every field not named there is discarded the moment the row is cached, so fatherName/motherName were being dropped one line before rcResultsCache ever saw them. The {...st} spread that DOES preserve them (further down, the secondary path) is a different function and is not what the Report Card calls. Confirmed schema from the user: results/<Course>_Sem<Roman>_<Year> -> regular[i].fatherName / motherName, same for backlog[i]. Both keys are now named explicitly in that push, with ?? fallbacks for father_name/fathername/FatherName spellings since results.html owns the write side. NOTE the lesson for any future field: adding a key to the results docs is not enough, it must ALSO be named in this whitelist or it silently vanishes here. (2) THE REAL GAP: fatherName is authored by the UNIVERSITY and only exists once a result sheet is published, so a first-year / Sem I student legitimately has no upstream source at all -- no amount of resolver work can surface a value that was never written. New manual store at app_data/student_parents { data: { URN: {f,m} } }, edited from a new PARENT NAMES button on the Report Card toolbar: paste three tab-separated columns straight out of Excel (URN, Father, Mother), Preview shows a parsed table flagging any URN not present in the current student list before anything is written, Export current downloads the saved set back out as .tsv for round-tripping. Parser also accepts comma or 2+ space separation and skips a URN/USN header row, because a hand-typed line is rarely tab separated. SAVE MERGES rather than replaces -- a bare set() of just the pasted rows would silently wipe the other 400 already stored, which is the obvious way this feature would have destroyed data on its second use. (3) PRECEDENCE, deliberate and stated: rcParentNames now reads result rows FIRST, the manual store second, allStudents last. The manual value is a stand-in for missing university data, so it must never overwrite a real published one -- the day results arrive the correct name takes over automatically and the manual row simply stops being consulted, no cleanup needed. The returned object carries a .manual flag so a future UI can badge a hand-entered name if that is ever wanted. Loaded once at login next to rcPhotosReady (rcParentsReady) and awaited by rcRenderCard exactly like photos, so no render races the fetch; saving re-renders the open card in place. CODE_BUILD=1122.

## v1120 · 17-Aug-2026 IST

FIX (reported live with a screenshot: the v1119 Widget Version card AND the top health banner both insisted "You are on w98, latest is w122" on the very phone that was physically running w122). ROOT CAUSE: davan_pub/widget_apk_report is keyed by the widget APK’s own 6-char pair code, which lives in the APK’s SharedPrefs. A fresh install or clear-data WIPES those prefs, so getPairCode() mints a BRAND NEW code and the widget starts reporting under it -- while this browser’s localStorage davan_widget_pair_code still holds the OLD code from whenever the widget was last tapped. Nothing ever deletes the old node, so it stays in RTDB frozen at whatever build was installed back then (w98 here), and every read against the stale code returned that number. Note the auto-resolver was simultaneously correct: it scans ALL report nodes and had already found the real w122, which is why the same banner could say "latest is w122" while claiming the device was on w98 -- the two numbers came from different nodes. FIX: new wcpReadOwnApkReport() reads the node AND AGES IT. A live widget rewrites its report on every fetch (periodic job = 30 min), so a report whose ts is hours old cannot belong to a running widget; ts, not apkVersion, is the trustworthy field. WIDGET_REPORT_STALE_MS = 6h (12 missed cycles) is deliberately generous so a phone merely asleep or offline is never wrongly flagged. A report with no ts at all is also treated as stale, since it cannot be aged. Both surfaces now route through this helper and, when stale, print NO version number at all -- the card reads "Re-pair" in amber and the banner adds an explicit line -- because showing the real-but-orphaned number is worse than showing nothing: it looks entirely credible. Both tell the user to tap the home-screen widget once (which re-pairs via ?wdev=<newcode>) and reload. Implementation caveat recorded: the stale flag is computed early in wcpCheckWidgetHealth but its banner line MUST be pushed after `const lines = []`, since touching lines before that declaration is a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError that would silently kill the entire banner. CODE_BUILD=1120.

(2) SECOND BUG found while fixing, would have broken the very next release: the 6h sha cache was keyed on age ALONE, so uploading a new APK and logging in would serve the cached sha and publish a URL pinned to the PREVIOUS binary. Cache entry now also stores ver and is discarded when the resolved apkVersion differs, since a version change is proof the file moved. ## v1117 · 17-Aug-2026 IST

AUTO-RESOLVED APK RELEASE INFO (user request: "cant it be auto") -- removes BOTH hand-edited numbers v1116 still required per release. New wcpResolveLatestApk(), memoized once per page load and awaited by both wcpPublishLatestApk() and wcpCheckWidgetHealth() so they can never disagree. (1) apkVersion is now the MAX apkVersion across all of davan_pub/widget_apk_report/* -- every APK w95+ already writes its real BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE there on every fetch, so the highest number in the field is by definition the newest build installed anywhere, and the existing habit of installing a fresh build on the admin phone first IS what publishes it to everyone else. The LATEST_APK literal is kept as a FLOOR only (never resolves downward, so a wiped or re-paired estate cannot drag the ceiling backwards) and APK_VERSION_CEILING=400 rejects absurd self-reports from a corrupt or hand-edited node, which would otherwise nag the entire estate into a permanent loop. (2) apkUrl is now the raw.githubusercontent URL PINNED TO THE LATEST COMMIT SHA of DavanWidget.apk, resolved via the public GitHub commits API -- sha-pinned raw content is immutable, so the whole stale-cache problem the v1116 ?v= buster worked around stops existing rather than being worked around. Verified against live headers before choosing this: raw.githubusercontent.com sends access-control-allow-origin:* (so the browser fetch is permitted) but NO Last-Modified, and its ETag is not a CORS-safelisted response header, so neither could be read from JS -- the commits API is the only header-independent way to get a content identity. sha cached in localStorage for 6h (davan_apk_sha_cache) because the unauthenticated API allows 60 req/hr PER IP and a campus of faculty shares one NAT address. Every failure path degrades to exactly v1116 behaviour: literal floor version + ?v=<version> buster. NET EFFECT ON WORKFLOW: build -> upload DavanWidget.apk to the repo -> install it on your own phone once; nothing in this file is ever edited for a widget release again. CODE_BUILD=1117.

## v1103 · 11-Aug-2026 IST

Generalized the v1102 admin-only fix to every faculty, per user request to check whether the same bug could hit them too -- confirmed it genuinely could. ## v1086 · 10-Aug-2026 IST

TWO FIXES in Faculty Class Alerts, both reported by the user from real screenshots. (1) Alerts Enabled and Live Toast checkboxes appearing unchecked after every new build. The static HTML never had a checked attribute, so the boxes render unchecked at first paint and only flip on after facAlertInit() finishes its async Firestore read -- on a fresh build or slow connection that gap is visible, and the underlying default object had enabled:false with no toastEnabled key at all, so any load failure (the catch block silently swallowed errors) would leave both features looking and actually being off with no visible warning. Fixed at three layers: the checkboxes now default to checked in the raw markup so there is no unchecked flash before Firestore responds; the in-memory faConfig default changed to enabled:true, toastEnabled:true so a failed or missing config document can never silently disable alerts; and facAlertInit() now logs load failures via console.warn instead of an empty catch, with the checkbox assignment changed from faConfig.enabled to faConfig.enabled !== false so only an EXPLICIT saved false unchecks it, never an undefined value from a partial load. (2) The WhatsApp status broadcast (facAlertWASummary) listed faculty like Priyanaka V and Smita under Working properly even though the subscription table right next to it showed a red notif off flag for them -- the summary only ever checked PWA-install plus subscription existence and never looked at the widget-level notifOn signal (_faWidgetReports, joined from davan_pub/widget_apk_report, already surfaced correctly in the on-screen table since v1005) that reflects whether the faculty has actually toggled Android notifications off for the widget -- a real, separate failure mode from being subscribed or PWA-installed. Added a fourth bucket, Notifications OFF on their device, using the exact same faculty-name resolution fallback chain the table already uses so the two surfaces can never disagree; a faculty with notifOn===false is now excluded from Working properly and Browser only and placed in this new bucket instead, with its own footer instruction line explaining that re-subscribing will not fix it -- they need to re-enable notifications in their phone Settings for the widget app. CODE_BUILD=1086.

## v1072 · 08-Aug-2026 IST

Found the REAL WhatsApp bug via console screenshot -- it was never the secure-context/HTTPS issue v1071 guarded against. Actual sequence: [CAR PDF] html2pdf() blob generated, size: 80399 (success!) immediately followed by [CAR WA] promise chain threw: TypeError: n.resolve is not a function, meaning PDF generation completed fine but something in the promise chain immediately after it crashed. Root cause: html2pdf.js's Worker object (returned by window.html2pdf()) is a custom thenable that mimics .then()/.catch() but is not a real native Promise -- chaining a plain .finally() onto it after .then()/.catch() threw from inside html2pdf's own minified internals, which do not correctly implement finally() on this bundle version. FIX: removed .finally(() => container.remove()) entirely from _carDownloadPDFInner()'s html2pdf chain; container.remove() is now called explicitly inside both the success branch (after building the return value) and the .catch() failure branch instead, since only .then()/.catch() are demonstrably reliable on this Worker object (confirmed by the blob having generated successfully before the crash). No functional change to output -- PDF still generates and downloads/shares identically -- this only fixes the crash that was happening immediately afterward during cleanup. v1071's secure-context guard and diagnostic logging are kept, since they are still correct/useful for actual HTTPS-related failures, just were not the cause this time. ## v1067 · 08-Aug-2026 IST

Added deep diagnostics to carDownloadPDF() to actually identify why window.jspdf never registers on the affected device, per explicit request to find the exact cause instead of continuing to guess. A <script src> tag onerror only ever reports pass/fail with zero detail -- CORS blocks, network failures, wrong MIME type, and DNS failures are all indistinguishable from each other via that API. Added a parallel fetch() of the identical CDN URL (mode:cors, cache:no-store) purely for diagnostics: logs the real HTTP status/statusText, response type (opaque vs cors, which reveals CORS blocking specifically), content-type and content-length headers, actual body length, whether the body text contains "jspdf"/"html2pdf" (catches a corrupted/truncated/wrong file being served), the first 120 characters of the response (catches an HTML error page being served instead of JS, e.g. from a captive portal or proxy), and on failure the real thrown error name+message (TypeError: Failed to fetch vs a CORS-specific message are very different diagnoses). Also logs navigator.onLine and location.protocol/href up front, timing (ms) for both the script tag and fetch attempts, and if window.jspdf is still missing after the UMD-registration grace period, dumps every plausible alternate global (window.html2pdf, window.jsPDF) plus whether the script element is still in the DOM -- covers the case where the bundle loaded but one of its internal dependencies (html2canvas) threw during its own init and prevented jspdf from ever being assigned. ## v1064 · 08-Aug-2026 IST

Found the REAL root cause via v1063's console trace: "[CAR PDF] script tag onload fired" followed immediately by "ok: false" on every single attempt -- meaning the html2pdf.js file WAS downloading successfully every time (no onerror, no CORS block, no timeout) but window.jspdf.jsPDF was not present the instant onload fired. Two compounding bugs, both fixed: (1) onload fires the moment the file finishes downloading, but a UMD bundle's module-registration code (the part that actually assigns window.jspdf) can run one tick later -- checking synchronously inside the onload handler was racing that registration. (2) Re-injecting a <script src="..."> with the exact same URL on retry can be silently ignored by some browsers/caches, which would explain onload firing identically on all 3 logged attempts while nothing changed -- now tags the injected script with data-car-pdf-lib, removes any stale one before injecting a fresh one, and appends a cache-busting ?_r=<timestamp> query param on every attempt so a retry is guaranteed to be a real re-fetch, not a served-from-cache no-op. ## v1050 · 28-Jul-2026 IST

FIX: auth/quota-exceeded (Firebase password-verification quota) hit during bulk report-card photo uploads. ROOT CAUSE: _ensureAuth() (called once per photo inside _rcSavePhotoToFirebase, itself called per-file in bulk uploads) has no lock — if firebase.auth().currentUser was momentarily null when a bulk upload started (page reload, tab backgrounded, token refresh gap), every single photo in the batch independently called auth.signInWithEmailAndPassword() with the cached admin credentials in parallel, since none of the concurrent calls saw currentUser set yet (that only happens after each call's own await resolves). A batch of 50-100 photos could fire 50-100 real password-verification attempts in the same few seconds, tripping Firebase's quota. This only affects admin flows since _ensureAuth() is only called from report-card/bulk-upload code (rcDoSingleUploadPanel, rcDoBulkUpload, rcPushAllPhotosToFirebase) — faculty/student logins never call it. FIX: added a shared in-flight promise (_ensureAuthInFlight) — if a re-auth is already in progress, subsequent concurrent callers now await the SAME promise instead of starting their own signInWithEmailAndPassword call, collapsing any number of concurrent _ensureAuth() calls into at most one real Auth request. CODE_BUILD=1050.

## v1048 · 27-Jul-2026 IST

FIX: Semester Dates saved in the student portal (student_portal.html ▸ Controls ▸ Semester Dates) kept reverting after every calendar edit here (e.g. adding a holiday). ROOT CAUSE: _autoPushCalendarToPortal() runs automatically after any calendar save and used lpDb2Set (Firebase PUT = full node overwrite) to push the in-memory SESSION_CONFIG object to davan_pub/session_config — the SAME path the student portal's Semester Dates control writes to. SESSION_CONFIG defaults to a hardcoded placeholder (10 Jul–11 Nov 2026) whenever this screen's own Session Config editor hasn't been used that session, so the auto-push was blind-overwriting real saved dates with that placeholder on every single calendar edit. Fixed two ways: (1) added lpDb2Patch (Firebase PATCH = merge, not replace) and switched the calendar auto-push to use it, so it can no longer wipe fields it doesn't send; (2) added window.SESSION_CONFIG_IS_DEFAULT, true until _applySessionConfig() loads/receives a real saved config — while true, the auto-push omits startDate/endDate from its payload entirely rather than pushing the placeholder. The deliberate "Activate & Go Live" write (_scfgDoActivate, explicit admin action with real staged dates) is unchanged — only the silent automatic push was the problem. CODE_BUILD=1048.

## v1035 · 24-Jul-2026 IST

FIX: Live Class Board (sN times ctN) badge was missing on I YEAR cards (BCom, BBA, BCA) while showing fine on II and III YEAR cards. Root cause: lcbTtClassToStudentClass always mapped I YEAR to Sem2, II YEAR to Sem4, III YEAR to Sem6, a hardcoded Even-semester-only rule left over from before the app-wide Odd/Even sem convention fix (v818 to v821, which established Odd equals Sem I, III, V and Even equals Sem II, IV, VI via getSemsForType). The current live session is 2026-27 Odd, so I YEAR students are really Sem1, not Sem2, and since I YEAR students are new admissions this term with no prior Sem2 record to fall back on, the ctMap lookup key never matched and the badge silently disappeared. II and III YEAR cards happened to still show a badge only because those students carry over an old Sem4 and Sem6 record from being I and II YEAR last academic year, so the wrong hardcoded key still matched something, just not necessarily the current sem attendance. Fix: lcbTtClassToStudentClass now reads SESSION_CONFIG.semType at call time and computes the sem number as year times 2 minus 1 for Odd or year times 2 for Even, matching the same convention already used by getSemsForType and getTypeForSem elsewhere in the app, with a safe fallback to the old year times 2 behavior if SESSION_CONFIG has not loaded yet so it never throws or returns blank. CODE_BUILD=1035.

## v1031 · 24-Jul-2026 IST

FIX: Faculty Subscription Status panel showed nonsense durations like 1970h ago for some subscriptions. Two bugs in the shared fmtAgo helper (three separate copies in the push-subscription and widget-status sections): (1) it never scaled to days, so anything over 24 hours old just kept counting hours indefinitely -- a subscription from a while back could show a huge hour count instead of a sensible day-and-hour figure. (2) a corrupted or implausible timestamp close to the Unix epoch (1970) -- likely an old subscription record stored before subscribedAt was consistently populated, or a stray value in seconds instead of milliseconds -- passed the existing falsy check since it was a small nonzero number, and produced exactly this 1970h ago symptom. Fixed both: all three fmtAgo copies now scale properly (just now, Nm ago, Nh ago, then Nd ago or Nd Nh ago past 24 hours), and any timestamp before 1 Jan 2020 is treated as unknown, blank, rather than displayed as a bogus multi-decade duration.

## v1030 · 24-Jul-2026 IST

FIX: Subscribe This Device showed a raw, confusing browser error (Script URL scheme is not http or https) whenever the app was opened as a downloaded file from disk (file:///C:/Users/.../index.html) instead of the real hosted site. This is a hard browser security restriction on service workers -- they can never register from a file:// origin under any circumstance, so no code change could make the actual registration succeed there. Added an early check in facRegisterSW() for location.protocol equal to file: that shows a clear, actionable message instead of letting the raw browser exception reach the user: push notifications do not work when opened as a local file, use the actual hosted link instead. This also explains the consoles Cross-Origin Request Blocked and other file:// related errors seen in the same session, all downstream symptoms of the same root cause -- running from a downloaded copy rather than the deployed site.

## v1026 · 24-Jul-2026 IST

Two real bugs from a session sharing a device, plus a confirmed-good diagnostic. (1) CRITICAL: 'Remember me' unchecked did nothing -- opening index.html always silently re-logged in as whoever last signed in on that browser, regardless of the checkbox (confirmed: Manjappa, then Hemavati, then Kiran all bled through on the same device). Root cause, two independent mechanisms both hardcoded LOCAL persistence and unconditional credential caching, ignoring the checkbox entirely: (a) doFacultyLogin() and doFirebaseLogin() both called auth.setPersistence(...LOCAL) unconditionally -- Firebase's own session then survived full browser restarts no matter what the user chose. Now setPersistence follows remember: LOCAL when checked, SESSION (cleared when the browser/tab fully closes) when not. (b) doFirebaseLogin() ALSO wrote _davanAuthEmail/_davanAuthPw to localStorage unconditionally on every successful login -- _ensureAuth() (used for background admin tasks) reads these to silently re-authenticate whenever firebase.auth().currentUser is momentarily null, e.g. right after a page reload, which resurrected the previous admin session even after Firebase's own persistence would have expired it. Now gated on remember, matching how doFacultyLogin() already correctly handles this pair (v988). (2) Dashboard flashed a stale student count (e.g. 511 from a previous semester) for a moment before settling on the real current count (311) on every admin login. Root cause: onLoginSuccess loads allStudents from the localStorage cache immediately, before any network call, so the dashboard's first paint (wgtRenderAdmin/wgtRenderFaculty) rendered real widgets from a POSSIBLY STALE cached snapshot, then re-rendered correctly once loadFirestoreData()/_loadFromRTDB() resolved and called renderAll(). Added window._allStudentsConfirmedFresh, false until the real fetch succeeds; wgtRenderAdmin/wgtRenderFaculty now scope allStudents to [] during render (reusing the existing _outOfScope temporarily-empty mechanism) whenever data is not yet confirmed fresh, so Total Students/Avg Attendance/Shortage/Critical show a neutral loading state instead of a possibly-wrong number, then repaint correctly the instant real data arrives. (3) Confirmed the [LP vs Dashboard subject count] diagnostic (v1022) is working exactly as designed -- user-provided console output showed Dashboard(alloc) 57 vs LessonPlan 50, with an 8-subject and 1-subject diff that reconciles the gap exactly (50+8-1=57); flagged two likely source-data issues worth checking (Personality Development (SEC) vs Personality Development(sec)40/10 look like the same subject with inconsistent naming, and a bare "TS" entry with a lesson plan but no matching allocation) but made no code change since this is a source-data question, not a code bug. RULE reminder (again): version bumps must update CODE_BUILD + BUILD_TIMESTAMP, not just the static topbar span. CODE_BUILD=1026.

## v1021 · 22-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: Report Card said 'No previous semester results found' for a BCom Sem III student who genuinely has Sem I results (confirmed real data exists via student_portal.html, which displayed it correctly for the same URN). ROOT CAUSE: rcFetchResults's processSlot() compared URNs with exact-case equality ((s.urn||s.usn) === urn) instead of case-insensitively -- student_portal.html's equivalent function already normalizes both sides to uppercase before comparing, so it found the match while index.html silently missed it whenever the URN casing stored in a results doc differed from what was passed in (e.g. a different upload batch/tool wrote lowercase or mixed-case URNs). FIX: all URN comparisons inside rcFetchResults (both processSlot definitions -- main Firestore path AND the RTDB fallback path used when Firestore permission is denied -- plus collegeRank/classRank lookups and the globalPool construction that feeds them) now normalize to uppercase before comparing, matching student_portal.html's existing correct behavior. CODE_BUILD=1021.

## v1018 · 22-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: v1017's new summary chips showed a phantom extra semester (e.g. 'Sem II: FAIL' chip + doubled Total Failed Subjects count) for a student who only had ONE semester of results actually rendered on screen. ROOT CAUSE: rcFetchResults() never deduplicated results[] by (course, sem) -- if the same real semester matched the student across more than one Firestore results doc/batch (e.g. present in BOTH a regular array in one doc and a leftover backlog array in another, or a batch scraped/uploaded twice), each match became its own separate entry. This was always possible but silent/harmless before v1017, since nothing summed across every entry -- the new chip totals were the first thing to make a silent duplicate visibly wrong. FIX: results deduplicated by course+sem before returning, preferring a non-backlog record over a backlog one when both exist for the same semester. CODE_BUILD=1018.

## v1015 · 22-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: Report Card / Results tab / WhatsApp still showed raw subject codes (KAN-B-2, IC-II, ENGL-S-2, BCA-2-4 etc.) instead of resolved names even after RC_SUBJECT_CODE_NAMES and LM_ALLOCATIONS.resultsCode were populated with correct data. ROOT CAUSE: rcLooksLikeCode() only recognized DSC-/DSE-/SEC-/BBC- prefixed codes and the 21BCAxxx pattern -- it did not recognize KAN-B-2, IC-II, ENGL-S-2, BCA-1-1, or any other code family. When a Firestore results record had the raw code duplicated into its own name field (sub.name === sub.code, common for records saved before a resolver existed), rcResolveSubjectName's hint check wrongly accepted the code AS IF it were a real name and returned it immediately -- short-circuiting before RC_SUBJECT_CODE_NAMES or LM_ALLOCATIONS.resultsCode were ever consulted. FIX: rcLooksLikeCode rewritten from an enumerated prefix list to a general structural heuristic -- real subject names are human prose (2+ spaces, contains lowercase); real codes are short, space-free/near-space-free, all-uppercase-and-digit tokens (<=14 chars after stripping separators). Verified against 16 real codes and 12 real names -- all correctly classified. CODE_BUILD=1015.

## v1015 · 24-Jul-2026 IST

CRITICAL fix: Lesson Plan panel (admin + faculty dashboard) was showing stale prior-semester subjects (e.g. "AFM", 98% done, updated_at ~02-Jun) as separate cards alongside this term's real subject for the same faculty/course (e.g. "Financial Management", 7% done, updated_at 24-Jul). ROOT CAUSE: v1014's claim that _lpFilterByAY was a "downstream call site" that "inherits the fix untouched" was WRONG -- it was silently inverted instead. _lpFilterByAY (v1009) used _legacyDataInScope()===true as its signal to skip the recency filter and show the full unfiltered historical blob (the archive-view case). v1014 changed _legacyDataInScope() to always return true for the live view too (to stop it blanking Dashboard/Students/Absentees/etc.) -- which meant _lpFilterByAY's "show everything unfiltered" branch now fired on EVERY view, live included, so the v1009 recency filter never ran again and every stale LP entry ever scraped kept showing next to fresh ones. ## v1006 · 11-Jul-2026 IST

ADMIN LOGIN & SESSION MONITOR (Admin Settings → 🔐 Login & Session Monitor). Because the app uses ONE shared admin password, everyone authenticates as the same Firebase uid — so monitoring/blocking is per-DEVICE, not per-person (the honest ceiling under a shared credential; true per-person control needs separate admin accounts). Each browser gets a stable random davan_device_id in localStorage. On every admin/manager/VP login, asmRegisterSession() writes davan_pub/admin_sessions/<devId>={role,name,device,loginAt,lastSeen,ua} and heartbeats lastSeen every 60s; a device is "online" if lastSeen < 2 min. The panel lists all devices with status/role/device/login-time/last-seen and a per-device Block/Unblock button. BLOCKING: asmBlock() sets davan_pub/admin_blocklist/<devId>=true; every session checks this on login AND on each 60s heartbeat via asmIsBlocked(), and a blocked device is force-signed-out (asmForceLogout: clears stored creds + sets logged-out guard + signs out) within ~1 min and cannot auto-login again. You cannot block the device you are currently on (guard). asmClearStale() prunes records offline >30d. asmEndSession() stamps loggedOutAt on logout. Recommended intruder response: Block the unknown device here AND change the admin PIN below (since the password is shared, blocking one device does not stop someone re-using the password on a NEW device — the PIN change does). All nodes under davan_pub (already client-writable); no security-rule change required, but for hardening consider restricting admin_blocklist writes to admin in Firebase rules later. CODE_BUILD=1006.

## v997 · 11-Jul-2026 IST

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (via v996 debug instrumentation, live device log) for the admin-session-bounce: it is CROSS-TAB CONTAMINATION, not a race condition in this tab. Firebase Auth LOCAL persistence (kept intentionally — needed so "Remember me" survives closing the whole browser, per requirement) broadcasts sign-in state to every tab of the same origin via a storage event. Proof from the v996 log: fire #4 (uid→null) and fire #5 (uid→admin, email=admin@davan.local) both arrived with document.visibilityState=hidden — this tab was in the background — and fire #5 had ZERO local signInWithEmailAndPassword call in its stack (the wrapper added in v996 logs every local call; none fired for admin in that session). This means a SEPARATE tab/window on the same device, already signed in as Admin, was open at the same time as Priyanka login; that other tab own Firebase Auth activity (e.g. periodic token refresh) rebroadcast "admin is signed in" to all tabs, and onAuthStateChanged in Priyanka tab applied it unconditionally, overwriting her live session ~30s in. Fix: onAuthStateChanged now checks — if a DIFFERENT user is already actively signed in in THIS tab (currentUser set, uid differs from the incoming broadcast, and this is not an in-progress manual login in this tab) — the incoming broadcast is ignored and logged as [AuthDebug] ... IGNORED — cross-tab broadcast. A session already active in a given tab now always wins over a signal arriving from another tab/window; deliberate account-switching within the SAME tab (sign out, then manually log in as someone else) is unaffected because doFacultyLogin()/doFirebaseLogin() set _isManualLogin=true before signing in, which the new guard explicitly allows through. LOCAL persistence itself was deliberately left unchanged — switching to SESSION persistence would have also fixed the symptom but would break multi-day "stay logged in after closing browser," which is required. Debug instrumentation from v996 (the [AuthDebug] fire-log and signInWithEmailAndPassword stack-trace wrapper) is left in place, harmless and useful if any related issue resurfaces. CODE_BUILD=997.

## v995 · 11-Jul-2026 IST

ROOT CAUSE FOUND for "faculty logs in successfully, dashboard loads, then ~2s later session silently reverts to admin": a stale davan_remember_admin_pw + davan_remember_user pair left in localStorage from a PAST admin session that was never explicitly signed out via the Sign Out button (only doFirebaseLogout() clears those two keys — closing the tab or navigating away does not) arms a setTimeout(…,1200) on every single page load that calls doFirebaseLogin() if !currentUser. The guard only checked currentUser at fire-time, but doFacultyLogin() did not set the _isManualLogin flag until AFTER its first await (the login_index Firestore fetch) — so during that fetch + the subsequent Firebase Auth round-trip, currentUser was still null and the stale-admin timer could win the race, sign the faculty user back out, and sign in as admin instead, ~1.2s after page load (which typically lands a second or two after a faculty member finishes clicking Sign In and seeing their dashboard). Fix: (1) _isManualLogin = true now set as the FIRST executable line of doFacultyLogin(), before any await, closing the race window entirely. (2) All early-return paths inside doFacultyLogin() (no login_index configured, no password match, admin-blocked-on-faculty-tab ×2, profile-missing, too-many-requests) now explicitly reset _isManualLogin = false so a genuinely stale timer is not permanently blocked after one failed/redirected attempt. (3) The admin auto-login setTimeout itself now re-checks currentUser, _isManualLogin, AND the davan_user_logged_out sessionStorage flag at fire-time (not just currentUser), with a console.log at each abort/proceed branch labeled [AutoLogin] so this exact race is visible in DevTools console if it ever recurs on a device. NOTE: this only fixes the RACE; the underlying stale-credential problem (any device where admin once used "Remember me" and never clicked Sign Out will keep re-arming this 1200ms timer on every load, indefinitely) still exists and is a separate, lower-priority cleanup — consider expiring davan_remember_admin_pw after N days or requiring re-confirmation. CODE_BUILD=995.

## v994 · 10-Jul-2026 IST

ROOT CAUSE FOUND for "VP note synced but a class with a dot in its name (e.g. I YEAR B.Com, II YEAR B.Com, III YEAR B.Com) never actually reached RTDB, even on v993": Firebase Realtime Database forbids the characters . # $ [ ] / in key names. v993's per-key RTDB write (rtdb.ref("davan_pub/class_notes").update({[cls]: text})) used the raw class name AS the RTDB key — for a class like "I YEAR B.Com", that key contains a literal dot, so the update() call THROWS synchronously (Firebase validates keys client-side before sending anything over the wire). The existing try/catch swallowed this into a console.warn only — completely invisible during a VP's mobile session with no console open. Meanwhile the Firestore write for the same note (no such character restriction there) succeeded fine, which is why a class WITHOUT a dot (e.g. "II YEAR BCA (A)", tested live with the note "hello") synced correctly end-to-end while a dotted class silently failed at the RTDB step every single time — 100% reproducible per-class, not random/intermittent as it initially appeared across multiple test rounds. This also explains why davan_pub/class_notes never appeared as a node in the RTDB tree at all in earlier checks: multiple of the college's actual class names contain dots (all three B.Com year-classes), so it was entirely plausible for every attempted write up to that point to have hit a dotted class name and failed before the node was ever created. Fix: added _rtdbSafeKey()/_rtdbUnsafeKey() — encodes forbidden characters into a reversible placeholder (e.g. "." → "__DOT__") ONLY at the RTDB read/write boundary, applied in all four RTDB touch-points: ttSetNote()'s per-key update, ttSyncLocalNotesToCloud()'s bulk update, the v982 manager/VP login hydration read, and the v990 admin-side RTDB-to-Firestore backfill read. localStorage and Firestore keys are completely unchanged (Firestore has no such restriction, and touching the localStorage key format risks breaking ttGetNote() retroactively for every class) — the raw class name is used everywhere except the literal RTDB key itself, decoded back to the real name immediately after any RTDB read. Verified round-trip correctness against all actual class names in LM_CLASS_META, including all three dotted B.Com classes. CODE_BUILD=994.

## v993 · 10-Jul-2026 IST

CRITICAL cross-device data-loss fix in Class Notes. Root cause of "VP synced their note, admin still sees a different/old note (e.g. leftover test text like ff)": ttSetNote() and ttSyncLocalNotesToCloud() both did a FULL .set(notes) overwrite of the entire app_data/class_notes doc + davan_pub/class_notes RTDB path, built from THIS DEVICE’s own local copy of ALL classes’ notes. If a device’s local copy was stale for even ONE class it never touched (e.g. leftover test text from an earlier session), saving or syncing a note for ANY OTHER class on that device would silently replace the entire cloud map — including classes it never touched — with its own stale local version, clobbering another user’s just-synced note for that class. This is precisely what happened: VP synced a real note for "I YEAR B.Com", then a save from a device with a stale local "ff" for that same class overwrote it, even though that device only meant to edit a different class. Fix: (1) ttSetNote() now writes ONLY the single changed class key — Firestore via .set({[cls]:val}, {merge:true}) (or FieldValue.delete() when cleared), RTDB via .update({[cls]:val}) (or null to delete a key without touching siblings). (2) ttSyncLocalNotesToCloud() (the manual Sync button) switched from .set(notes) to .update(notes) [RTDB] / .set(notes,{merge:true}) [Firestore] — still pushes everything on this device, but merges key-by-key instead of replacing the whole doc, so it can only ADD/update keys this device has, never silently delete a class note this device doesn’t know about. (3) The v990 RTDB-to-Firestore backfill (loadFirestoreData) now writes ONLY the specific recovered keys via merge:true, not the whole merged map, for the same reason. Net effect: two people can now edit two different classes’ notes at the same time on different devices and NEITHER can ever silently destroy the other’s work — the failure mode that caused this bug is now structurally impossible, not just less likely. CODE_BUILD=993.

Diagnostics: ttSetNote() now console.logs every step of a class-note save \u2014 (1) confirms the note text + class it wrote to localStorage, (2) logs ✅/❌ separately for the RTDB write and the Firestore write, including "not initialized \u2014 write SKIPPED" if rtdb/db aren\u2019t ready yet. ## v990 · 09-Jul-2026 IST

Follow-up to v989\u2019s note-sync fix, for notes that were ALREADY typed on a pre-v989 build before the fix shipped. Scenario hit in practice: VP added a class note while their browser was still running v988 \u2014 on v988, ttSetNote() wrote ONLY to RTDB (davan_pub/class_notes), so the note reached RTDB but Firestore app_data/class_notes stayed empty for that class. v989\u2019s admin read only pulls from Firestore, so admin still saw nothing even after upgrading, because Firestore genuinely had nothing to give it \u2014 the note was RTDB-only from before the fix existed, and there was no automatic way to backfill it. Fix: loadFirestoreData() (admin login) now ALSO does a one-time RTDB read of davan_pub/class_notes on every admin login, merges in any class key that Firestore is missing/blank for (RTDB fills gaps only \u2014 Firestore still wins if both have a value, since Firestore is the newer authoritative store post-v989), writes the merged result back to Firestore so the gap is healed permanently after the first login, and shows a toast confirming how many notes were recovered. No manual action needed from the VP or admin \u2014 self-heals automatically the next time admin logs in, and stays self-healing going forward for any future case where a Firestore write silently fails but the RTDB one succeeds. CODE_BUILD=990.

## v989 · 09-Jul-2026 IST

Two fixes. (1) PERMANENT class delete: existing 🗑 (csDeleteClass) only ever HIDES a class — the LM_CLASS_META key stays in the database forever, which is why ghost duplicates like "I BBA" kept silently reappearing after being "removed" (hide is cosmetic, not deletion; only 🔀 Merge actually deletes a key). Added a new ⛔🗑 button per Class Settings row → csHardDeletePrompt()/csHardDeleteClass(): checks LM_TIMETABLE and LM_ALLOCATIONS for any entries belonging to that class first; if either has data, refuses and points to 🔀 Merge instead (so real data can never be silently lost by this button); if genuinely zero timetable + zero allocation entries, deletes the LM_CLASS_META key with a full overwrite to RTDB + Firestore (same durable-delete pattern as csMergeClasses) and cannot be undone. Re-checks data counts again immediately before the actual delete in case something changed between prompt and confirm. (2) Class Notes sync gap: v982 added RTDB note sync but only wired the hydration read into _loadFromRTDB() (the manager/VP login path) — loadFirestoreData() (the ADMIN login path) never fetched app_data/class_notes at all, so a note a VP typed reached RTDB but an admin logging in via Firestore never pulled it into their own localStorage, and ttGetNote() (localStorage-only read) kept returning empty for admin. Also, ttSetNote() only ever wrote to RTDB, never to Firestore, so even the admin path had nothing to read even if wired up. Fixed both: loadFirestoreData() now also fetches app_data/class_notes and merges it into localStorage (merges onto, not overwrites, in case a note was just saved seconds earlier on the same device); ttSetNote() and ttSyncLocalNotesToCloud() now write to BOTH RTDB davan_pub/class_notes AND Firestore app_data/class_notes on every save, so admin and manager/VP logins both read a note regardless of which store the other role wrote it to. ## v988 · 09-Jul-2026 IST

Root-cause fix: faculty/VP login (e.g. Anitha N) would appear to sign in successfully then, within about a second, silently sign back out and restore an ADMIN session instead — happened without ever explicitly logging out of admin first. Cause: doFirebaseLogin() (admin sign-in) caches the admin email+password into localStorage (_davanAuthEmail/_davanAuthPw) so _ensureAuth() can silently re-authenticate for background admin tasks (Cloudinary uploads, report-card bulk ops) after a page reload. doFacultyLogin() never cleared these keys, so if an admin had signed in on that browser earlier (even in a prior session, without logging out via the Logout button) and then Anitha signed in via the Faculty tab, any subsequent code path calling _ensureAuth() would find firebase.auth().currentUser temporarily falsy, read the STILL-CACHED admin credentials, and silently re-sign-in as admin — overwriting her session. Fix: doFacultyLogin() now clears _davanAuthEmail/_davanAuthPw immediately after a successful faculty/VP sign-in, so no stale admin credential can ever resurrect an old admin session mid-way through a different session. Separately fixed umRebuildLoginIndex(): the rebuilt login_index.users objects were missing the role field entirely (only name/username/password were mapped), which is read by doFacultyLogin() as a secondary admin-block check and as a profile-reconstruction fallback — now includes role: u.role || ROLE_FULLTIME. CODE_BUILD=988.

## v959 · 06-Jul-2026 IST

Fixed KAN Hours-Check showing an inflated/wrong count (e.g. KAN 6/4 ↑ with the HIN chip missing) whenever a class has BOTH plain "Kan" cells and plain "Hin" cells (not just a combined "K/H" period). ## v958 · 05-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: Dr. Shilpa R Y (and any other faculty in FACULTY_NAME_ALIASES) photo not showing anywhere despite a successful upload. Root cause: facPhotos is keyed by exact normalized name text; Staff Directory has her as "Dr. Shilpa R Y" (upload key "dr. shilpa r y") but other surfaces (allocation/timetable-driven screens) reference her via the aliased legacy form "Shilpa R Y" (key "shilpa r y") — two different keys pointing at the same person, so the photo saved under one was invisible under the other. Fix: new _facPhotoUrl(key) helper (built on a lazily-built normalized _facAliasKeyMap from FACULTY_NAME_ALIASES) tries the exact key, then its alias, before falling back to initials. CODE_BUILD=958.

## v957 · 05-Jul-2026 IST

Fix (real root cause): facUploadPhoto REUSED the same Cloudinary public_id (built from the faculty name) on every upload. First-ever photo for a faculty always worked (nothing to collide with); CHANGING an existing photo repeatedly failed with no error message — because unsigned upload presets cannot overwrite an existing asset at the same public_id, so Cloudinary silently rejected/ignored the replacement. Confirmed via user report: "only when it comes to change the photo I have prob" (first upload fine, re-upload stuck on old photo, no toast at all). Fix: public_id now includes a timestamp (name + Date.now()) so every upload — first OR replacement — always creates a brand-new distinct Cloudinary asset and can never collide. v955/v956 fixes (cache-busting URL, honest DB-save error reporting) both still apply on top of this. CODE_BUILD=957.

## v956 · 05-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: facUploadPhoto() showed "✅ Photo saved." even when the Firestore write (app_data/faculty_photos) failed — the failure was only console.warn-logged, not surfaced. This meant a faculty photo re-upload (e.g. Hemavati Desai, reported still showing old photo after v955 cache-bust fix) could succeed on Cloudinary + show briefly in the current tab (facPhotos[key] updated in memory), but silently fail to persist — so the OLD photo came back on next login/reload via facPreloadPhotos() re-reading the un-updated Firestore doc. Now a DB save failure returns null and shows the real error message (e.g. permission-denied) instead of a false success toast, so the actual cause is visible instead of looking like a caching problem. CODE_BUILD=956.

## v955 · 05-Jul-2026 IST

Fix: Staff Directory photo upload appeared to do nothing — re-uploading a faculty photo (e.g. Hemavati Desai) kept showing the OLD image. Root cause: facUploadPhoto() saved Cloudinary secure_url as-is; since uploads always target the same public_id per faculty (built from their name), the browser cached the image by that URL and never re-fetched after a new upload. Fix: facUploadPhoto() now appends a cache-busting ?v=<timestamp> to the stored URL on every successful upload, forcing a fresh fetch. CODE_BUILD=955.

## v951 · 06-Jul-2026 IST

Fixed lab variants showing no faculty for multi-word lab codes like OA - Lab. Root cause: the friendly-lab parser regex required the base to be a single alnum word ([A-Z][A-Z0-9]*), so OA - Lab A1 Lab 1 (base has spaces + a hyphen + the word Lab) failed to parse as a lab and lmBaseCode returned the whole string, so no allocation matched. Fixes: (1) lmParseCode friendly-lab regex now accepts ANY base before the batch token, so OA - Lab A1 Lab 1 parses to base OA - Lab, batch A1, lab 1. (2) tteGetPickerOptions, _ttCellFacName and lmAllocMatchesCode now use parsed.base (not lmBaseCode) for lab slots and also compare against the raw allocation code, so a lab slot matches an allocation whose code is literally OA - Lab. Result: every OA - Lab A1/A2 x Lab 1/2 option shows the correct faculty (with photo) in the dropdown, the under-cell name label fills in, and the SAME faculty sees each lab slot at its time in their own faculty schedule. Since one teacher handles all batches/rooms, allocating that single OA - Lab row is enough - all four variants inherit that faculty automatically. Non-lab and K/H matching unchanged. CODE_BUILD=951.

## v948 · 05-Jul-2026 IST

Fixed lab hours double-counting. A 2-hour lab fills 2 consecutive slots PER BATCH, and both batches (A1, A2) run the same lab (parallel in the two lab rooms, or on different days). Previously the Hours-check summed all lab cells into one number, so A1 (2 slots) + A2 (2 slots) showed 4/2 OVER against a target of 2. Now lab cells are tallied PER BATCH: each batch is checked against the weekly target independently and they do not sum. So target 2 means each of A1 and A2 must fill 2 slots; when both have, the chip shows 2/2 done (not 4/2). The chip now also shows a per-batch breakdown, e.g. DBMS 2/2 (A1 2/2, A2 2/2); under is shown while any batch is short (e.g. A2 1/2), over if any batch exceeds the target. Non-lab subjects and the K/H combined count are unchanged. CODE_BUILD=948.

## v911 · 03-Jul-2026 IST

(4) All timetable saves (ttSave, activation, fsSet) now write ttSemKey + davan_timetable_semkey stamp. (5) Activation clears/stamps the timetable per your rule: allocation carries over (odd→odd/even→even via existing clone), timetable starts EMPTY for the new AY for admin to build. Verified: seed AY→253 slots (no disruption), new AY no-data→EMPTY, new AY saved→loads its own, stale old cache→ignored. ## v896 · 29-Jun-2026 IST

Fixes 2 of 3 reported bugs. (1) FIXED — Live Class Board & dashboard timetable widgets: added isSemOver() helper; when today > SESSION_CONFIG.endDate, lcbRender() shows a "Semester Completed" card and wgtTodayClasses()/wgtNextClass() return "Sem Over" instead of stale timetable. ROOT CAUSE confirmed: davan_pub/widget_active_user (read at Tier-0, line 500) is a SINGLE GLOBAL RTDB node, not per-device. Every login from any phone overwrites it, so all widgets follow whoever logged in last. The APK Tier-0 read DEPENDS on this node existing — removing the PWA write (first v896 attempt) would break the widget to a permanent "Please log in" state, so that attempt was reverted. Proper fix requires a coordinated PWA+APK change: key the node per-device as widget_active_user/<devToken> on both write (PWA) and read (APK). Hold widget changes until APK v89 ships the matching read.

## v882 · 29-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Batch override on a slot (e.g. changing col-0 from III B.Com to II BBA, selecting subject, saving) was lost on reload — the slot appeared as III B.Com with no subject. Root cause: INT_SLOT_BATCH_OVERRIDE is reset to {} on every load, and was never restored from saved Firestore data. intBuildSlotsGrid then rendered all columns with their default batch names, ignoring the saved II BBA slot entirely. Fix: Added two-pass override restore at the start of intBuildSlotsGrid — Pass 1 marks columns whose default batch has a saved slot (no override needed). Pass 2 finds columns with no default-batch match and assigns them the next unmatched saved batch_name as an override, exactly restoring the user's per-slot batch changes.

## v881 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Safety: Nuclear guard added inside fsSet() itself -- any call to fsSet(app_data, students, {data:[]}) from ANY code path is now blocked at the lowest level with a console stack trace identifying the exact caller. ## v880 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Safety: 3-layer student data protection. (1) _safeWriteStudents() helper: blocks any write of 0 students to Firestore/RTDB and auto-checkpoints the previous live data to app_data/students_checkpoint before every overwrite. (2) All 3 student write paths (auto-sync, post-scrape, Sync to Cloud) now call _safeWriteStudents() so an empty array can never silently wipe the database again. (3) Emergency Restore card in Admin Settings: one-click restore from the latest checkpoint.

## v879 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Root cause of No data on dashboard finally confirmed via v878 diagnostics — app_data/students Firestore doc EXISTS but data[] array is empty (0 students). loadFirestoreData checked studentsDoc?.data which is truthy for an empty array [], so it set allStudents=[] and returned without trying RTDB fallback. Fix: condition changed to !studentsDoc || !studentsDoc.data?.length — empty array now falls through to _loadFromRTDB() which correctly loads students from davan_pub/students in RTDB.

## v878 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Diagnostics: Added console.log to loadFirestoreData and _loadFromRTDB at every branch (doc not found, doc found with N students, RTDB path empty, all paths exhausted) so admin can see exactly why dashboard shows No data. This identifies whether app_data/students is missing in Firestore (needs portal scrape) vs RTDB empty (needs Sync to Cloud) vs localStorage cleared. No logic changes.

## v877 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Dashboard Total Students / Avg Attendance / Shortage / Critical still showing "No data" after v875/v876. Root cause: both _sanitizeRtdbKeys (auto-sync) and _sanKeys (manual Sync button) bailed out early on arrays — "if Array.isArray(obj) return obj" — so the "regular" array of student objects was returned unsanitized, leaving subject keys like "B.COM-3.2" (with dot) intact and causing Firebase RTDB to throw "invalid key". Fix: both functions now recurse into arrays with .map(), ensuring every nested object at any depth has its keys sanitized before writing to RTDB.

## v876 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: B.COM-3.3 key error still thrown in v875 — a second copy of the results-to-RTDB sync (inside the manual Sync to Cloud button handler at line ~15096) was missed in the v875 fix. Both copies now use _sanKeys() to sanitize dots and illegal chars in all Firestore result doc keys before writing to RTDB.

## v875 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Admin auto-sync Results step was throwing "invalid key (B.COM-3.3)" because Firebase RTDB disallows dots in keys. Results Firestore docs use subject keys like B.COM-3.3, B.COM-3.4.M etc. Added _sanitizeRtdbKeys() recursive helper that replaces . # $ / [ ] with _ before writing to davan_pub/results. This was causing the auto-sync to abort early, leaving dashboard stats as No data on login.

## v874 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Re-fill from Template and Rebuild both filled only morning slots (09:30, 11:30) and left all afternoon slots as — select —. Root cause: template matching used time_label equality (e.g. "01:15pm to 02:15pm") — when 2nd internal has different afternoon times than 1st internal, no template slot matched. Fix: both intRefillFromTemplate and intRebuildSlotsGrid now match by SLOT POSITION within session (slot 0, 1, 2…) not by time_label. Template slot 0 afternoon → fills slot 0 afternoon of 2nd internal regardless of actual time.

## v873 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix (Bug 1): usedSubs in intSlotBatchChange still showed already-used subjects as selectable. Root cause: intCollectSlots was looking up slot IDs by default batch name (b.name) not the overridden batch name — so overridden slots were invisible to usedSubs computation. Fix: intCollectSlots now reads INT_SLOT_BATCH_OVERRIDE per column index to resolve the effective batch name before building the slot ID. Fix (Bug 2): intRefillFromTemplate produced wrong layout when called — it was rebuilding the grid ignoring all batch overrides and showing scrambled data. Fix: now resets INT_SLOT_BATCH_OVERRIDE before rebuilding so the grid starts clean from the template.

## v872 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: After switching batch in a slot cell, the subject dropdown showed already-used subjects as selectable instead of struck-through. Root cause: intSlotBatchChange used an empty usedSubs Set. Fix: now calls intCollectSlots from the live DOM to compute usedSubs cross-date for the new batch — same logic as intBuildSlotCell at render time.

## v871 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Batch dropdown in slot cells only showed batches already in the session list — III BCA and others were missing. Now shows all keys from INT_BATCH_MAP so any class can be selected for any slot column.

## v870 · 28-Apr-2026 IST

User can change it to any other batch in the same session (e.g. III BCA → II BBA), and the subject dropdown immediately reloads with subjects for the newly selected batch. ## v869 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Refresh button (↻) next to internal selector was missing its id="int-edit-refresh-btn", so spinner/disable feedback never worked. Added id. Added toasts throughout intEditLoad: "Fetching from Firestore…" on load, "Restoring unsaved draft…" on draft restore, "Draft restored ✓" / "Loaded: <title> ✓" on success, "Document not found in Firestore" / "Firestore error — showing cached data" / "Firestore error — no cache available" on failure. Spinner (…) and disabled state now correctly applied and reset in all code paths.

## v868 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Changing a slot time caused ALL other slots on that date to show '00:undefinedam' and lose their data. Root cause (1): the time <input> used onchange which fires on EVERY intermediate state while the user is still typing — partial values like empty string or '00:' were passed to intUpdateTimeSlot, causing INT_EDIT_TIMES[date] to be corrupted with invalid entries. Root cause (2): no validation guard in intUpdateTimeSlot, so any invalid value was blindly written and sorted into the times array, then intFmtTimeLabel(invalid) produced garbage labels for all rebuilt rows. Fix: (1) Changed onchange to onblur so intUpdateTimeSlot fires only when the user leaves the input (complete value). (2) Added regex validation guard at top of intUpdateTimeSlot — rejects anything that is not a valid HH:MM string before touching INT_EDIT_TIMES.

## v867 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Subject saved to Firestore appeared as green border (value set) but showed blank in the dropdown. Root cause: if existingVal was in usedSubjectList (subjects used on other dates), it was rendered as a disabled+struck-through option with selected attribute — browsers do not honour selected on disabled options, so dropdown showed blank. Fix: if existingVal is in usedSubjectList, needsCustom=true → renders it as a separate enabled+selected option above the used list, making it display correctly.

## v866 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: intFixSessionSlots (count-based slot repair) was running during intBuildSlotsGrid (Firestore load path). If dirty data had been saved (e.g. extra/different slots from previous edit bugs), the count-based repair added phantom slots like 04:30 PM that were never in the original data. Load path now uses PRESENCE-ONLY guard: only adds a session if the date has ZERO slots for that session (safe). The count-based intFixSessionSlots runs only on explicit Rebuild Grid and Re-fill from Template actions where the user has intentionally asked for slot correction.

## v865 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Changing a slot time wiped all subjects for that slot. Root cause: intUpdateTimeSlot called intRefreshDateBlock which called intCollectSlots — but intCollectSlots looks up DOM dropdowns by key=(date|newLabel|batch), and the DOM still had elements keyed on the OLD label. New label = no match = blank subjects. Fix: intUpdateTimeSlot now (1) snapshots subjects from DOM BEFORE updating INT_EDIT_TIMES using old labels, (2) updates+sorts times, (3) remaps subjects from old label to new label by slot index position, (4) rebuilds date block with remapped subjects so all dropdowns are pre-filled correctly.

## v864 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: Re-fill from Template still did not restore 01:30pm slot for 2026-05-07. Root cause: the session guard checked "does this date have ANY afternoon slot?" — 15:30 passed the check so 13:30 was never restored. Introduced shared helper intFixSessionSlots() that compares the afternoon SLOT COUNT of each date against the reference date, not just presence. If counts differ, replaces the entire session portion with the reference pattern. Applied in intBuildSlotsGrid, intRebuildSlotsGrid, and intRefillFromTemplate.

## v863 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix: intUpdateTimeSlot was doing a label-only DOM update (updating the span text) instead of rebuilding the full date block. When a slot time was changed in a way that flipped its session (e.g. 01:30pm → 09:30am), the row still showed the old session batch columns. On save+reload, the stored time_label was reinterpreted with the new time, causing the slot to show under the wrong session or vanish. Fixed by calling intRefreshDateBlock(date) from intUpdateTimeSlot — also sorts INT_EDIT_TIMES[date] after the edit so slots remain in chronological order.

## v862 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix (Bug 1): intBuildSlotsGrid (called on initial load from Firestore) did not apply any session guard. If afternoon slots were deleted before saving for a specific date, that date loaded with morning-only INT_EDIT_TIMES, causing afternoon rows to never render. Added a 2-pass approach: Pass 1 reads saved time_labels per date; Pass 2 uses cross-date reference — finds another date that HAS the missing session and borrows its exact slot pattern (e.g. 13:30+15:30), instead of blindly adding all 4 defaults. This prevents showing extra unwanted slots like 02:30pm and 04:30pm.

## v862 · 27-Apr-2026 IST

Fix (Bug 2): intRebuildSlotsGrid and intRefillFromTemplate were using INT_DEFAULT_TIMES (all 4 afternoon slots) when restoring missing session slots. If the internal only used 2 afternoon slots (13:30, 15:30), clicking Re-fill from Template showed 4 afternoon rows instead of 2. Fixed both functions to use the same smarter cross-date reference: find another date that has afternoon data → borrow exactly its afternoon times → only fall back to all 4 defaults if no date in prevTimes has afternoon data at all.

Now always fetches fresh from Firestore on every dropdown switch. Cache still updated after each fetch; fallback to cache with warning toast if Firestore fails. Added ↻ Refresh button next to the internal selector dropdown as manual fallback — calls intEditLoad(true) which skips draft restore check too.
